location: BLACKHURST CULTURAL CENTRE
description:
📚Three days of books and ideas that reflect who we are!

The Black & Caribbean Book Affair 2026 returns to Blackhurst CC from Oct 15–17th under the theme Seeing Ourselves: The Next Chapter.
🔹Oct 15 | 6–8 PM
Dr. Carl James discusses Seeing Ourselves: Exploring Race, Ethnicity & Culture, 5th ed., with educators M. Proudfoot and A. Dualeh.
🔹Oct 16 | 6–8 PM
Ramie Veerappan joins S. Whiting for a conversation about Ramie’s Dance of Resilience: Apartheid and Beyond, by Romila Logarahjah-Jeevithan.
🔹Oct 17 | 9–10 AM on Zoom: Gelien Matthews and Rhoma Spencer discuss Calypso Rose, who broke through the male-dominated calypso world.
11 AM–1 PM: A Parade of Children’s Books with Heather Beaumont, Delano Brown and host Yolanda Marshall.
4:30–6:30 PM: Didier Leclair launches The African Prince, the Translator, and the Nazi in conversation with Canute Lawrence.
Join us as Black & Caribbean stories take centre stage!📚

title: Ancient Circuitry (X Avant XXI: Memory Mannnnn, Night 3)
location: First Unitarian Church,473 Oakwood Ave, York, ON M6C 2R5, Canada
description:
Gathering two artist’s projects in concert form, Ancient Circuitry combines Mani Mazinani’s Solar Organ and Alexis Nanibush-Pamajewong’s For The Youth: Reilluminated, connecting with ancestral knowledge today.

Solar Organ Ensemble moves between improvised and composed music using traditional and invented pentatonic scales covering a spectrum of approaches to pentatonic sound generation. Solar Organ https://manimazinani.net/project.html?project=Solar-Organ , an electronic pentatonic instrument created by Mani Mazinani, connects neurobiology with the geographic and historic ubiquity of pentatonic practice, a universal human phenomenon.

For The Youth: Reilluminated by Alexis Nanibush-Pamajewong, is a re-creation of a light and sound installation https://www.instagram.com/alexisnanibush_pamaj/p/DQngD8REaYa/?img_index=2 with local Indigenous youth performances — to honour the life, kinship, and the spirit of generations past, present, and future.

Curated by Mani Mazinani

INSTALLATION
Outside of performances, attendees can interact with sound sculptures from Night 2 https://musicgallery.org/events/flashback/ artist Stephanie Orlando.

Inspired by everyday sounds from her time working as a bike mechanic, Stephanie Orlando’s Sonic Bikes installation invites attendees to interact with the spectrum of noises and musical textures of recycled bike parts.

All prices are inclusive of HST.

title: Question Everything: Evaluating in an era of bias, spin and social polarization
description:
Part of the Think, Research, Create: Intro to Library Research Series (3 out of 4)
Not all information is created equally—and not all search tools work the same way. This interactive workshop will help you compare popular tools for information discovery from AI to academic search platforms. You’ll learn the differences between misinformation, disinformation, malinformation, AI hallucinations and deepfakes. We’ll show you practical fact-checking tools and strategies to help you figure out what’s real and what’s not. You’ll also practice evaluating sources, including academic ones, so you can choose the most reliable information for your assignments. By the end, you’ll feel more confident navigating the information jungle!

title: Wilder Series: The Even Wilder Loop
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/wilder-loop-fall-26)**
**We're heading somewhere new, and it's wilder than anything else in the series.**
This is the first time WU is running the Even Wilder Loop, and it's the next step up in our Wilder Series, our lineup for those chasing bigger days out. The name isn't subtle. This is a remote, rugged backcountry in a less visited part of the park, and you'll feel it from the first kilometre.
The trail climbs and drops hard in places, with some scrambles along the way where you'll need your hands as well as your feet. Between the climbs, it opens onto barrens and meadows, and you'll see plenty of beaver dams along the way.
Partway through, the river crossing takes us through some rapids.
It's only 8.5 km, but it's some of the wildest 8.5 km we run.
***Secret Location***
This is one of Wilderness Union's 'secret' hikes. As a group, we visit some truly special spots that are undiscovered by the wider world. We like to keep them pristine and only share them among our members - we ask that you do the same! We reveal the location to registered members in the days before the trip.
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**The Rapids Crossing:** The most memorable stretch of the day. You will get wet!
**Wildlife Spotting:** Bears, moose, beavers and loons are just some of the creatures that call this area home. You'll have a chance to spot some from a safe distance for a magical encounter.
**A WU First:** Nobody in the crew has done this loop with us before. You'll be part of the first group on it.
**Itinerary**
**07:00** \- Shuttle leaves from near Keele station
**10:00 - 15:00** \- Hike loop at secret location
**15:00** \- Anticipated return to cars
**18:00** \- Anticipated return to Toronto
**Event cost: $66+HST. $50+HST optional transport also available. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/wilder-loop-fall-26)**
**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.
Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.
Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!
***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: SOLD OUT: Birding with Beni: Fall Birding
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fall birding nature walk!
Fall migration is well underway! Join TBG Horticulturist and avid birder Sasan Beni for an engaging walk through the gardens and Wilket Creek Ravine, as you seek out the wildlife that call this place home. Learn how to identify the many different species passing through and how you can help them in their journey.
 
Bring your binoculars for a better view (we will have extras on hand) and a mug/thermos for a warm beverage and post-birding chat.
 
As with any wildlife tour, the spotting of birds and other wildlife is not guaranteed and is not within the control of the tour guide. Please be patient and considerate. The tour will not be rescheduled due to a lack of bird sightings. The tour will only be rescheduled due to inclement weather.
 
Meet at the TBG main entrance, just outside the George and Kathy Dembroski Centre for Horticulture.
 
Saturday, October 17, 8 to 10 a.m.
Public $22, Members $20 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Sasan Beni
Sasan Beni is a writer turned horticulturist. He graduated with a diploma in Environmental Landscape Management from Seneca College in King City, worked for the Toronto Zoo as a seasonal gardener, and joined TBG in 2020 as a seasonal Horticulturalist. His home is a revolving door of tropical plants. Beni is also passionate about birdwatching and wildlife photography. In the last three years, he has led many guided birdwatching walks around Toronto and has written several articles for Trellis magazine illustrated with his nature photographs.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Accessibility
The walk will be at a leisurely pace throughout, following designated pathways and trails but sometimes covering uneven terrain and steep inclines. Dress appropriately for the weather and walk slowly. Wearing layers is recommended. Closed-toed shoes are required. We will begin promptly. 
NOTE: This program occurs rain or shine (save for cases of extreme weather); please dress appropriately for the weather.
 
Additional Program Information



Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.
To learn more about the Toronto Botanical Garden and our programs, please review our list of Frequently Asked Questions.

title: 🚐 Doors Open Niagara-on-the-Lake Road Trip!  Saturday, October 17
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
**🚐 Doors Open Niagara-on-the-Lake Road Trip!**
**Saturday, October 17**

Let’s hit the road for another Doors Open adventure! We’ll be heading to beautiful **Doors Open Niagara-on-the-Lake** to explore historic buildings, cultural sites, and hidden spaces that are rarely open to the public.
Nick has been a **Doors Open Toronto volunteer for over two decades**, and he always enjoys checking out Doors Open events in other cities. Niagara-on-the-Lake is known for its incredible heritage architecture, charming streets, and fascinating history—making it a perfect destination for a Doors Open day trip.

***

### 🏛️ What is Doors Open?

If you’ve never attended before, **Doors Open** is a free architectural and cultural event held in communities across Ontario. For one special weekend, cities open the doors to historic buildings, cultural institutions, churches, theatres, and other interesting spaces—many of which are normally closed to the public.
Visitors can explore at their own pace, learn about local history, and sometimes go behind the scenes with guided tours or special access.

Learn more about the event here:
👉 [https://www.doorsopenontario.on.ca/pages/events/niagara-on-the-lake](https://www.doorsopenontario.on.ca/pages/events/niagara-on-the-lake)

***

### 🗓️ The Plan

* **Departure:** 8:00 AM from just outside **Christie Station**
* **Transportation:** Rental minivan or SUV
* **Destination:** **Niagara-on-the-Lake**
* Spend the day exploring **Doors Open sites around town**
* Time permitting we may be able to visit Niagara Falls after for a few photos/sightseeing
* **Return to Toronto:** Around **6:00 PM**, depending on traffic

You’re welcome to explore with the group or wander off to check out sites that interest you most. The day will be relaxed and flexible.

***

### 🍽️ Food & Drink

You are responsible for **your own food and drink purchases** throughout the day.

***

### 💰 Cost

**$60 round-trip**
This covers:

* Car rental
* Insurance
* Fuel

To secure your spot, **all participants must e-transfer $60 to:**
📧 **[nicolasbello@yahoo.com](mailto:nicolasbello@yahoo.com)**
Spots are limited based on vehicle capacity, so please RSVP only if you’re able to commit.

***

### 🌦️ Weather Note

This event **runs rain or shine**, so please **dress appropriately for the weather**. The good news is that we’ll be **inside most of the time**, but there will still be some walking between locations.

***

### 🎒 What to Bring

* Comfortable walking shoes
* Curiosity & good vibes
* A little patience for traffic (it’s part of the road-trip charm!)

Join us for a fun architectural adventure and a chance to explore one of Ontario’s most historic towns. 🚐🏛️

description:
TechTO
**This is a paid event. You must register and have a ticket to attend.** 🎟️ **Tickets are on Luma:** [Get your ticket here](https://luma.com/hackathon-oct-17-2026?utm_source=meetup)

**Eat. Code. Ship. Win 💲**
We’re back with another 12-hour build day on October 17 for builders, dreamers, and doers. We provide the food, the mentors, and the prize pool.

**🎯 The Mission**
Build an AI agent that finds and books the best deal at a hotel in City X. Every agent runs the same task at the same time. The fastest and cheapest booking wins.

**📋 The Rules**

* No ready-made agents
* No browser automation tools
* Agents must make a phone call and receive a receipt at a provided email address
* Bring your friends, public models, and APIs

**What’s Included**

* 🤝 Work alongside 100+ ambitious coders, developers, and designers. You might just meet your next coding buddy.
* 🏆 Compete for cash prizes and cloud credits.
* 👥 No team? We got you! We kick off the morning with a team-matching session to pair you with fellow builders.
* ☕ Complimentary coffee, lunch, dinner (pizza), and drinks are included with your ticket.

**📝 Agenda**

* **10:00 AM \| Hacking Begins:** 7 hours of uninterrupted building. Lunch at 1:00 PM.

* **7:00 PM \| Awards & Celebration:** Winners announced, followed by a networking social until 9:00 PM.

description: Dates : Saturday and Sunday October 17-18 & 24-25 2026 Times : 10:00am - 4:00pm Location : 300 Campbell Avenue, Unit 115 Instructor : Janet Macpherson Unlock new creative possibilities in ceramics with our comprehensive Mold-Making 101 course. This hands-on class will guide you through the process of designing and creating plaster molds for both slip casting and press molding techniques. You’ll learn how to craft one-part and two-part molds, make decorative sprig molds, and combine slip-cast pieces into finished ceramic forms. Throughout the course, you'll explore: - The fundamentals of plaster and its use in mold-making. - Techniques for creating and using press molds and sprig molds. - How to design and construct two-part molds for more complex shapes. - The basics of slip casting and assembling multi-part pieces. - Finishing techniques to prepare your work for firing and glazing. You can book a glazing session seperately ($50) by emailing the technician at our Dupont Location. Glazing sessions include the use of our studio glazes. Firing fee is included. 2) Due to the hands-on and cumulative nature of this course, it's important to attend each session as we may not be able to repeat material covered in a missed class in a thorough way although we will try to catch you up. 3) By the end of the course, you'll have developed a new set of skills, a collection of unique molds, and the confidence to continue exploring mold-making in your own creative practice. title: 🍂 Fall Walk of Toronto Island 🌊🌆! 9KM
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🍂🌊 FALL WALK: TORONTO ISLANDS 🌊🍁

### Island Paths, Fall Colours & Toronto's Best Urban Escape

There is something magical about the Toronto Islands in the fall.
Once the summer crowds disappear, the islands become quieter and more peaceful. The changing leaves, crisp air, open green spaces, quiet cottages, and golden light over the water make it one of the best times of year to explore.
And then there's the skyline.

From the islands, you get some of the best views of Toronto anywhere in the city — especially when the fall colours frame the downtown skyline across the water.

Join us for a relaxed fall walk through **Hanlan's Point, Centre Island, and Ward's Island**, enjoying the scenery, fresh air, and great conversation along the way.
This is approximately **9 km**, with mostly flat paths and no major hills. It's a longer walk, but the pace will be relaxed and we'll take breaks along the way

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 🚶‍♂️ What We'll Do

We'll take the **10:15 AM Ward's Island Ferry** and begin our walk once we arrive.

Our route will take us through:
🌿 Hanlan's Point
🍂 Centre Island
🏡 Ward's Island
📸 Skyline viewpoints
🌊 Waterfront pathways
🍁 Fall foliage and quiet island roads

We'll stop along the way to enjoy the scenery, take photos, have a snack, and spend some time getting to know each other.

Although we'll pass several beaches, **we won't be stopping at them during this event**. We have a route to follow and a ferry to catch!

Our return ferry will be the **2:45 PM Ward's Island Ferry** back to downtown Toronto.

Expect approximately **3½ to 4 hours**, including the ferry rides and breaks.

***

## 🍁 Fall Weather & Expectations

The islands can feel quite different from downtown Toronto, especially in the fall. Expect cooler temperatures, wind off the lake, and changing weather.
Please dress in layers and bring a jacket or sweater.
This is a **social walk, not a guided historical tour**. I'll share interesting facts along the way, but the focus is enjoying the islands together.

***

## 🧢 Meetup Details

📍 **Meetup Location:** **INSIDE the Jack Layton Ferry Terminal after your ticket has been scanned.**
We are meeting **inside the paid waiting area beside the washrooms.**
**Please do NOT wait outside the terminal.**

Once your ferry ticket has been scanned, walk into the waiting area and you'll find me wearing my **Moose Hat**. 🫎

⏰ **Meetup Time:** **10:00 AM**
🚢 **Ward's Island Ferry LEAVES AT:** **10:15 AM**

Please be on time. **Once the ferry leaves, it will be extremely difficult to catch up with the group.**
🚢 **Return Ferry:** 2:45 PM from Ward's Island
🎟️ **Ferry Ticket:** $9.19

You must purchase your ferry ticket **before signing up for the event.**
[CLICK HERE FOR FERRY TICKETS](https://secure.toronto.ca/FerryTicketOnline/tickets2/index.jsp)

***

## 🎟️ Meetup Fee

**$5 cash in person or e-transfer**
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**
This fee helps support the group and allows us to continue organizing events throughout Toronto.

***

## 🎒 What to Bring

💧 Water
👟 Comfortable walking shoes
🥨 A snack
🧥 A warm fall jacket or sweater
🕶️ Sunglasses
📸 Camera or phone for photos

***

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This walk is great for:

* Anyone who loves fall 🍂
* People who enjoy exploring Toronto's parks
* Anyone looking for a longer but easy walk
* People who enjoy beautiful scenery and photography
* Anyone who wants to meet new people
* People who want to escape the city without actually leaving it

The activity is the container. **The people you meet along the way are the real experience.**

***

**Come for the island paths.**
**Stay for the fall colours.**
**Leave feeling like you spent the day on vacation — without ever leaving Toronto.** 🍂🌊

You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.
Sometimes plans change and events may need to be cancelled, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**

Questions? Post on the event wall or email:
📧 **torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com**

title: Hurricane Hazel 2026 (SPECIAL ANNIVERSARY EDITION)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

On October 15, 1954, Toronto was devastated by the deadliest Hurricane of the 1954 season. Hazel was the most intense hurricane to hit the continent of North America in 1954.

Prior to the disaster that struck Toronto, the storm killed 469 people in Haiti, and the Caribbean before striking the United States. It roared ashore as a Category 4 hurricane.

After causing 95 deaths in the US, Hazel struck Ontario, raising the death toll by 81, mostly in Toronto. As a result of the high death toll and the damage caused, its name was retired from use.

But Toronto gained so much from the 1954 disaster, and our ravines and parklands are our lungs of the city. Thanks to Hazel we have our green spaces for generations to come.

This walking tour is for all levels and walkers with a few small hills and some steps. The tour begins outside the Weston Branch of the Toronto Public Library at Weston Road and 2 King Street, and returns to the starting location at the end of the walk. TTC bus routes are adjacent.

title: Wildlife-friendly Fall Gardens
location: Toronto Reference Library, Room B1 (located in the basement)
description:
At this time of year, many people admire the fall colours but also feel the need to rake and dispose of leaves, cut dead stems, and remove fallen branches. But what if this tidying up negatively affects our gardens and pollinators? While we may not see the bees and butterflies during the fall and winter, they are still around!

title: Virtual REGISTER: Phil Collins - The Solo Years Musical History
description:
Experience Toronto
**Important: When you sign-up, you will also need to Register as soon as possible** **to obtain your link to the event.**

On **Saturday October 17th**, enjoy the music of **Phil Collins - The Solo Years**, **focusing on his career as a solo artist (as opposed to his time with Genesis) during the 1980’s and 1990’s.** During and after our program you’ll have the opportunity to participate in an online discussion with your fellow music lovers via Zoom. **Register for your virtual link of Phil Collins - the Solo Years. on Saturday October 17h at 3pm.**

**Philip David Charles Collins** (born 30 January 1951) is an English singer, drummer, songwriter, record producer, and actor. He was the drummer and later became the lead singer of the rock band Genesis and had a successful solo career, achieving three UK number-one singles and seven US number-one singles as a solo artist. In total, his work with Genesis, other artists and solo resulted in more US top-40 singles than any other artist throughout the 1980s. His most successful singles from the period include "In the Air Tonight", "You Can't Hurry Love", "Against All Odds (Take a Look at Me Now)", "One More Night", "Sussudio", "Another Day in Paradise", "Two Hearts" and "I Wish It Would Rain Down".

Collins's discography includes eight studio albums that have sold 33.5 million certified units in the US and an estimated 150 million records sold worldwide as a solo artist, making him one of the world's best-selling music artists. He is one of only three recording artists, along with Paul McCartney and Michael Jackson, who have sold over 100 million records both as solo artists and separately as principal members of a band. He has won 8 Grammy Awards, six Brit Awards (winning Best British Male Artist three times), two Golden Globe Awards, one Academy Award and a Disney Legend Award. He was awarded 6 Ivor Novello Awards from the British Academy of Songwriters, Composers and Authors, including the International Achievement Award. He received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1999, was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2003, the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of Genesis in 2010, and as a solo artist in 2026.

title: 🎬Documentary Movie: You Can See Everything -  Food & Drinks after the movie 🍿!
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🎬 Let’s Go to the Movies (and Actually Talk… or Not)

Whether you're a film nerd, popcorn enthusiast, or just looking for a chill night out with interesting people — this one's for you.

We’re heading out to see a movie together, then grabbing food or drinks after. If the film's great (or terrible), we’ll probably talk about it forever.

If it’s just okay, we’ll talk about it for 10 minutes and move on to everything else — books, dating apps, weird dreams, how Toronto keeps getting more expensive, etc.

The vibe is relaxed, friendly, and not too serious. No film degree needed. No icebreakers. No pressure to “perform.” Just come enjoy the film, connect with some thoughtful people, and see where the night goes!

🎞️ **Movie Title + Trailer:**[ \[Click here to watch trailer!\]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HvW_N5p1q44)

📖 **Plot Summary:** Thirty-four days before she's sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon soon becomes a mind-bending, three-year journey into the abyss.

***

### 🗓️ Event Details

📍 **Meetup Time:** 6:00 PM....I will only wait 5mins
🎬 **Movie Start Time:** 6:20pm
⏱️ **Runtime:** 3hrs
📌 **Meetup Spot:** I will be standing by the white stairs close to the Pickle Barrel by the Cinplex entre and I will be wearing my Moose Hat.

**📍 Please Meet Us at the Meetup Spot!**

Please meet us at the designated Meetup spot before heading into the theatre. This gives everyone a chance to say hello, meet fellow members, and chat before we take our seats. Once we're inside the theatre, it's much harder to mingle, so don't miss this opportunity to connect with the group before the movie!

🎟️ **Cost:**

* **$11.50** for *CineClub* members
* **$16.00** regular admission

👉 You are responsible for buying your own ticket.

**🪑 Reserved Seating:**
You must buy your ticket *before* signing up. You'll be asked where you're sitting so we can try to group everyone together! However, members are welcome to sit anywhere that works for them.
🎫 **Buy your ticket here:** [https://www.cineplex.com](https://www.cineplex.com/)
📍🪑 **Where I will be sitting:** I will be in ROW "I" SEAT "15"

🍿 **After the Movie — We Strongly Encourage You to Join Us!**

Yes, we're heading out afterward! It's not just a movie night — it's a social night.

We strongly encourage everyone to join us for food, drinks, or a chat after the movie, even if you can only stay for a little while. Some of our best conversations happen afterward, when we share our thoughts about the film, get to know one another, and make new friendships.

The movie brings us together, but spending time together afterward is often where those connections really begin. We'd love for you to be part of it!

***

### ✅ Before You Sign Up

* Please **buy your ticket first** — seating is limited!
* When signing up, let us know your **seat number** so we can try to group everyone together.
* You can still sign up or just **show up on the day** if you're not sure you can make it — we're flexible!

📲 **Join Our WhatsApp Group:** [Click here to join](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)
🎟️ **Join Cineplex’s CineClub for discounts:** [https://www.cineplex.com/cineclub](https://www.cineplex.com/cineclub)
🎁 **Get your SCENE Card** for free movies and points: [https://www.scene.ca](https://www.scene.ca/)

***

### 🎥 A Quick Word About Movie Etiquette

We love a great film experience. Please:

* Turn off your phone.
* Don't talk during the movie.
* Be respectful of others.

Repeat offenders will be removed from the group — we take our cinema seriously (but with snacks).

***

### 👥 About the Group

This event is open to everyone — single, not single, shy, social, new in town or a long-time local. We're a group for people who love movies *and* making real connections. We also do walks, hikes, restaurants, arts & culture — come be part of it!

🎬 **Organized by:** Mathew
📧 **Questions? Reach out:** [torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com](mailto:torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com)

Ever wish there were an easier way to turn a room full of strangers into people you actually want to talk to?

Instead of arriving at a busy pub and wondering who to approach, our host guides you through short conversations and rotations, giving you the chance to meet a variety of people throughout the evening. You get a little structure to make connecting easier — without making the evening feel forced or formal.

And once the hosted rounds finish, you can keep the evening going. 🎲
We’re back at Stout Irish Pub in Cabbagetown — a relaxed Irish pub with food, drinks and 50+ board games, giving you plenty of ways to continue socialising with the people you’ve met.

Throughout the evening, we’ll mix in themed rounds and interactive prompts designed to make connecting easier.
They’ll help you discover shared interests, experiences and unexpected things you have in common — taking the conversation beyond the usual small talk.

Stout’s current After Dark Special runs from 9–11 PM, with $7 beers and $7 highballs, among other specials.

Come for the conversations. Stay for the games. Leave with new connections. ❤️

title: Ishq Ke Saat Muqaam
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Ishq Ke Saat Muqaam (The Seven Stages of Love) returns with a renewed artistic vision, bringing together poetry, music, dance, and storytelling to explore one of humanity’s oldest and most profound questions: what does it mean to love?

Written and directed by Nishar Mansuri, the production is inspired by the Sufi understanding of ishq as a path of transformation. Through seven interconnected stages, the work moves from human longing to self-discovery, devotion, and surrender, inviting audiences into a journey that is both deeply personal and universal.

Featuring the poetry of Rumi, Amir Khusrau, Kabir, Bulleh Shah, Hafez, Fariduddin Attar, Sultan Bahu, and other mystic voices, the production reimagines centuries of mystical thought through contemporary performance. Their words become the foundation for an experience that transcends borders, languages, and faith traditions, inviting audiences to reflect on love as a force that connects us all.

title: Cliffs & Fall Colours: A Bruce Peninsula Hike
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/bruce-peninsula-26)**

**The Bruce Peninsula does dramatic better than almost anywhere else in Ontario, and fall is when it really shows off.**

We'll be out for most of the day, covering 8.5km of moderate hiking through some of the best autumn scenery in the province, with the changing leaves against the escarpment's limestone making for a proper contrast.

We'll start in the forest before the trail opens onto the coastline, tracing the cliffs down to the Grotto. It's the most photographed spot on the peninsula for good reason: crystal clear water, a sea cave carved into the rock, and a natural window out to the bay. We'll take our time here, including a stop for lunch.

From the Grotto we'll keep following the shoreline out to Stormhaven, crossing pebble beaches with open views across Georgian Bay the whole way. We'll turn around there and retrace the coastline back, catching all the same cliffs and colour from the other direction with the light shifted by then.

**Two important things to note:**

1. **Self driving isn't possible for this trip. Parking passes at the trailhead sell out well in advance, so all members travel together on WU transport.**
2. **Bruce Peninsula National Park is stunning, but be aware that it is a long drive there and back. Full details are in the itinerary below.**

**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com

**Highlights**
**The Grotto:** The peninsula's most famous natural feature: a limestone sea cave with turquoise water and a rock window looking out over Georgian Bay.
**Stormhaven Coastline:** A stretch of cobble beach with wide open views across the bay, well past where most day hikers turn around.
**Fall Colour on the Escarpment:** Peak autumn colour against the Niagara Escarpment's pale limestone cliffs, a contrast you don't get anywhere else on the Bruce Trail\*\*.\*\*

**Event cost: $140+HST. Transportation is included in the cost of the adventure. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/bruce-peninsula-26)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: Paper Quilling: Fall Tree Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Celebrate the magic of autumn with a relaxing day of creativity at the beautiful Toronto Botanical Garden!
Join artist Deepa Krishnan for a fun, beginner-friendly paper quilling workshop. In this 4-hour session, you’ll learn a variety of quilling techniques while creating a stunning fall tree on an 8”x10” canvas. Inspired by the rich colours of the season, you’ll have the freedom to choose your own autumn palette, making your artwork truly one of a kind.
 
This workshop includes a 30-minute lunch break. We recommend bringing your own lunch to enjoy while taking in the beautiful surroundings of the garden.
 
Whether you’re trying paper quilling for the first time or looking to expand your skills, this workshop is a wonderful way to slow down, get creative, and celebrate the beauty of the season.
 
All supplies are included, and no prior experience needed. This workshop is suitable for adults and children ages 12 and above.
 
Sunday, October 18, 10:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.
Public $100, TBG Members $90 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Deepa Krishnan
Deepa Krishnan is a self-taught artist specializing in the art of paper quilling, which involves manipulating narrow strips of paper to create exquisite designs. She discovered this art form when she was looking for a creative outlet from her engineering job. She was amazed by the possibilities and beauty of paper quilling, that she decided to pursue it as a full-time career. Since then, she has been passionately mastering this technique and has created many artworks drawing inspiration from nature, music and travel. She cuts the paper strips in different widths to add depth and dimension to her creations. She loves to play with the colours and experiment with the quilling techniques to create her own distinctive style. Deepa believes that anyone can learn this art form, regardless of their age or skill level, and she hosts many workshops to spread the joy of quilling. She enjoys seeing her students discover their own creativity and style in paper quilling.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: 🌿 FALL WALK -  Walk: Tommy Thompson Park (Come See The Skyline) 🐦 - 12KM
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🍂🐦 Fall Walk: Tommy Thompson Park 🌊

### Wildlife, Lake Views & One of Toronto's Best Fall Walks

Looking for a walk that feels like you've left the city without actually leaving Toronto?

Join us for a fall walk through **Tommy Thompson Park**, one of Toronto's most unique outdoor spaces.
The park is famous for its wildlife and birding, with **more than 300 species recorded**, as well as its beautiful views across Lake Ontario and back toward the Toronto skyline.
In the fall, the cooler air and quieter trails make this a particularly nice time to explore the park. We'll follow the trails toward the **lighthouse**, take a break along the way, and then make our way back.

It's a **long walk**, but the terrain is generally easy. The goal is to enjoy the scenery, get some fresh air, and spend a few hours walking and talking with other people.

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 🚶‍♂️ What We'll Do

We'll meet near the pavilion and begin our walk through Tommy Thompson Park.

Along the way we'll:

* Explore the park's trails 🌿
* Look for birds and other wildlife 🐦
* Enjoy views of Lake Ontario 🌊
* Take in the Toronto skyline 🌆
* Make our way toward the lighthouse
* Stop for a break and some photos 📸
* Loop back to the pavilion

The walk will take approximately **3 hours, including a break**.
This is a longer walk, so you should be comfortable walking at a steady pace for several hours.
**No dogs are permitted in the park.**

***

## 🍁 Fall Weather & Expectations

This is an outdoor walk, and Tommy Thompson can be exposed to the wind coming off Lake Ontario.
Please dress appropriately for the weather and bring comfortable walking shoes.

The trail isn't particularly difficult, but **the distance is the challenge**. If you're not comfortable being on your feet and walking steadily for around three hours, this may not be the right walk for you.

***

## 🧢 Meetup Details

📍 **Meetup Location:** Near the pavilion and bathrooms
🫎 **Look for me in my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time: 11:00 AM sharp**
I will only wait **5 minutes.**
**Early is on time. On time is late.**
🏁 **End Point:** Tommy Thompson Park Pavilion

***

## 🎟️ Meetup Fee

**$5 cash in person or e-transfer**
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**
This fee helps support the group and allows us to continue organizing events throughout Toronto.

***

## 🍔 After the Walk

Once we've finished, you're welcome to join us for lunch at **Wendy's or Tim Hortons** nearby.
It's completely optional, but it's a great chance to sit down, refuel, and continue the conversation after the walk.

***

## 🎒 What to Bring

💧 Water
👟 Comfortable walking shoes
🥪 A snack
🧥 A fall jacket or sweater
📸 Camera or phone for photos

***

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This walk is great for:

* People who enjoy nature and wildlife 🐦
* Anyone interested in birdwatching
* People who love waterfront walks
* Anyone looking for a longer social walk
* People who want to explore somewhere different in Toronto
* Anyone who enjoys getting outside and meeting new people

The activity is the container. **The people you meet along the way are the real experience.**

You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**

Questions? Post on the event wall or email **torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com**

**Come for the wildlife.** 🐦
**Stay for the conversation.**
**Leave with a new connection — and maybe a new friend.** 🍂💛

title: Impressionist Afternoon Tea + 3 Exhibits at the AGO
description:
Experience Toronto
On **Sunday, October 18th**, join me for an **Impressionist Afternoon Tea in the Norma Ridley Members’ Lounge to celebrate the connection between art, atmosphere and indulgence.** Inspired by the luminous colours and expressive brushstrokes of *[Impressionist Revolution: Monet to Matisse from the Dallas Museum of Art](https://ago.ca/exhibitions/impressionist-revolution-monet-matisse-dallas-museum-art)* we saw last month, this seasonal Afternoon Tea offers an elegant, leisurely escape into art, conversation and thoughtfully crafted flavours that reflect the beauty and softness of this exhibit. Delicate savoury selections and whimsical pastries are designed to evoke sunlit gardens, countryside picnics and the romance of Impressionism. Since Afternoon Tea includes free admission to the Gallery, we will see more Impressionism art that was not part of our August visit - **Reality & Reverie: Canadian and European Painting Beyond Impressionism**, **Steam: Impressionist Painting Across the Atlantic**, and a new exhibit that will open the day before - **In Plain Sight: Highlights from the AGO’s Collection of Historic Picture Frames**. **I** **have booked a table for Sunday October 18th at 2:30pm, and can add members to it.**

**COST**
Adult: $80 + taxes + gratuity = $104.80

Meetup Organizer Fee: $5

**SIGNING-UP**

* **RSVP Yes** **\- everyone goes on the waitlist until confirmed\.**
* **I will reach out to provide my email address for the etransfer of $109.80 and I will call in to add you to our table. Once I receive confirmation, I will inform you and move you to attending.**
* There are no refunds.

A reminder will be sent the day before with my cell and reminder details where to meet and when.

RSVPs close 3 days prior and the Waitlist will be removed at that time. Cancellations will result in a No Show and impact future attendance.

**MEETUP TIME**
**Meet me at: 1:45pm inside the entrance to the right side of the AGO at 317 Dundas St. W. We will then scan our tickets and head over to the exhibits, prior to Tea.**

**Note: We must enter the AGO together for our tea reservation.**

**EXHIBITS**
**Reality & Reverie: Canadian and European Painting Beyond Impressionism** (Level 1 Gallery 127)

**Steam: Impressionist Painting Across the Atlantic** (Level 1 Gallery 116)

**Highlights from the AGO’s Collection of Historic Picture Frames** (Level 1 Gallery 115)

title: The Historic Eastern Beaches! (NEW FOR 2026)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
[torontohistorywalks@gmail.com](http://torontohistorywalks@gmail.com%2A%2A/)
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***
\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
[torontohistorywalks@gmail.com](http://torontohistorywalks@gmail.com%2A%2A/)

**This tour is a revised route for 2026.**

The area was first settled in 1794 by the Ashbridge family, whose name is remembered by the nearby bay and park. Their homestead on Queen Street East was well to the west of the area currently identified as the Beaches. A later generation of the Ashbridge family rebuilt the family home in 1854 and can be seen on Queen Street East opposite the TTC barns near Kingston Road.

The Beaches remained a sparely settled community until the end of the 19th century when extension of the Grand Truck Railway, the draining of the northern parts of Ashbridges Bay, and the construction of street car tracks on Queen Street and Kingston Road, opened the area to settlement.

From Sunnyside Amusement Park built in 1922 to Scarboro Beach built in 1906, it seemed that Toronto cornered the market on summertime chills and thrills.

We had 5 major amusement parks along our waterfront, and two smaller parks, Victoria Park and Munro Park, virtually unknown to Torontonians today, but extremely popular summertime places, years ago as pleasure parks.

This walking tour is for all walking levels and fitness skills. Please dress for the season and bring water. And remember to bring your love of history.

It begins outside the Beaches Branch of the Toronto Public Library at Queen Street East, and Lee Avenue adjacent to Kew Gardens. The tour ends where we started, back at the library.

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
[torontohistorywalks@gmail.com](http://torontohistorywalks@gmail.com%2A%2A/)

title: Beginner Crochet - October
location: Bistitchual, 266 Jane St, Toronto, ON M6S 3Z2
description: This listing is for a two session Beginner Crochet Course. The classes will be held in person at Bistitchual on Sunday October 18th and 25th from 2:30pm-4:00pm Learn the fundamentals of crochet in this two part class. We will be covering chaining and single crochet, as well as double and half-double crochets. Don’t know what any of that means? Great, you’re in the right place! We’ll provide all the materials, including a simple pattern that teaches you common terms and instructions you’ll encounter in most crochet projects. We will also discuss how to choose the appropriate yarn and hook for a project as well as where you can take your crafting after you master these basic techniques. There’s a lot to learn, and we’re excited to accompany your beginning in the wonderful craft of crochet! Materials are included! - 50g ball of worsted weight cotton in your choice of colour - 6mm crochet hook Our class size is capped at 4 people, so everyone can receive the attention they need. Mike will share lots of tips and techniques to get you well on your way. About the instructor: Tired of disposing of clothes that were still perfectly wearable, Mike (he/him) started crafting mainly as a means of mending and repair. This led him to knitting (and later crochet), which pretty much immediately became one of his favourite tools of self-expression. Please note that classes will only proceed if we have a minimum of two attendees . If the minimum is not met, there will be the option for a refund or to reschedule. There will be a four person maximum for each class. Please pre-book your spot to let us know you are coming! Cancellation Policy Classes must be paid for at the time of registration to reserve your spot. - If cancelled 48 hrs or more prior to the start of the first class will be given a store credit. Thanksgiving is over, Halloween is almost here, and it's time to get out, meet some fun people, grab a drink, and enjoy some live comedy.

Please respect your RSVP. If you sign up, you're committing to attend because our tickets are limited and someone else could take your spot.

Want to join us but missed out on the four group tickets? You're still welcome! You'll just need to **book your own free tickets directly with Backroom Comedy Club**.

According to the club's invitation, there are only 12 free seats per show, and tickets are first come, first served. You must receive confirmation of your tickets before heading over.

Lectures & Snacks is your chance to mingle with fellow York grad and mature students over light refreshments while enjoying a short, engaging talk by a student, faculty or staff member. Think of it as a mini lecture with maximum curiosity…and snacks!

title: Dystopia Nonfiction Book Club: A Good War
location: Toronto Reference Library, Lower Level, Room B1
description:
Join us each month to discuss issues in politics and society, and explore how powerful forces are exploiting our world and dystopian imaginings are becoming present-day realities.
October’s book is
A Good War: Mobilizing Canada for the Climate Emergency
by public policy advisor Seth Klein. Copies of the book are available in print, eBook & eAudiobook format. Book club attendees are encouraged to read the book in advance of the meeting.
"In A Good War, Seth Klein explores how we can align our politics and economy with what the science says we must do to address the climate crisis. But Klein brings an original and uniquely hopeful take to this challenge. The book is structured around lessons from the Second World War – the last time Canada faced an existential threat. Others have said we need a “wartime approach” to climate change, but this is the first book to delve into what that could actually look like. Canada’s wartime experience, Klein contends, provides an inspirational reminder that
we have done this before
. We have mobilized in common cause across class, race and gender, and entirely retooled our economy in the space of a few short years."
Drop in. No registration required.

title: Rachel Sommerville (CCA, Flatiron Institute)
location: MP1318A
description:
Title: Turtles all the way down: towards a new paradigm for galaxy formation and cosmology

Abstract: A new generation of multi-tracer surveys has the potential to yield huge progress in our understanding of galaxy formation and cosmology, but only if we can overcome certain challenges. These include accurately modeling the intertwined effects of baryonic processes and the nature of dark matter and dark energy, as well as incorporating diverse types of data and observational tracers into a robust statistical framework. I will discuss how my collaborators and I are working towards building more robust, physically motivated sub-grid models for star formation, stellar feedback, and black hole formation and growth. I will describe the status of our efforts to use these new models to train accelerated forward models using machine learning, create detailed multi-probe synthetic observations, and fold all of these elements into a Simulation Based Inference pipeline, with the ultimate goal of constraining galaxy formation, cosmology, and the initial conditions that gave rise to our Universe.

title: Annual Howard Adelman Lecture: Immigration Exceptionalism and the Dual State
location: Helliwell Centre, Room 1014 @ 4700 Keele St, North York, ON M3J 1P3, Canada
description:
October 19, 2026
4:00pm – 6:00pm (ET/Toronto)
This is an in person event.
Attendance is free, but please RSVP  ( https://crs1.apps01.yorku.ca/machform/view.php?id=109949 )by October 15 2026
Location: Helliwell Centre, Osgoode Hall Law School, 1014 Osgoode Hall, Keele Campus
Guest Speaker: Audrey Macklin, Professor of Law and Chair in Human Rights, University of Toronto
Discussants: Deepa Nagari, PhD candidate in York University’s Socio-Legal Studies and Kushan Azadah, recent PhD graduate, York University
Abstract:
The second Trump Administration’s campaign of mass detention and deportation of non-citizens has prompted commentators to invoke of the theory of the Dual State developed by German Jewish lawyer Ernst Fraenkel.  The Dual State defined a bifurcated legal order emerging under the Nazi regime, one for ‘friends’ (the normative state) and the other for ‘enemies’ (the prerogative state).  My  presentation identifies the continuity between elements of the Dual State and immigration exceptionalism, through which all liberal democracies structure and justify the diminution or negation of non-citizens’ legal rights in the name of sovereignty.  I contend that Immigration exceptionalism greases the slide toward a dual state, and helps explain why the spectacular cruelty, arbitrariness, and violence directed at non-citizens is at the vanguard of President Trump’s authoritarian governance.
Bios:


Audrey Macklin is Professor of Law and Rebecca Cook Chair in International Human Rights. She studied law at University of Toronto (LLB 1987) and Yale Law School (1991), and clerked for Justice Bertha Wilson at the Supreme Court of Canada.  After commencing her academic career at Dalhousie Law School, she was appointed at University of Toronto in 2001 and called to the Bar in 2004.  From 1995-1997, Prof. Macklin was a Member for the Immigration and Refugee Board (Refugee Protection Division), and served as Director of the Centre for Criminology and Socioloegal Studies from 2017-2023.
Professor Macklin researches, teaches, advocates and publishes widely in the fields of migration, citizenship, refugee, and human rights law, as well as administrative law.  She is active in public-facing work that includes pro bono interventions at all levels of court, including the Supreme Court of Canada and human rights engagement in Canada and abroad.  She frequently appears in media in Canada and internationally on issues relating to migration, counter-terrorism, refugees, citizenship and business and human rights.  Her work has been cited numerous times by the Supreme Court of Canada.
Prof. Macklin is a Fellow of the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation, the Canadian Institute For Advanced Research (CIFAR), and recipient of the Carolyn Tuohy Award for Public Policy.




Deepa Nagari is a 5th-year PhD candidate in York University’s Socio-Legal Studies. Her research focuses on how asylum laws and policies (such as the US-Canada Safe Third Country Agreement) shape asylum pathways into Canada. She also explores how advocates, organizations, municipalities, and cities are adapting their services, policies, and advocacy to these rapid shifts.




Kushan Azadah is a political scientist and migration scholar whose work examines refugee governance, migration policy, and the contested boundaries of protection in Canada. He recently completed his PhD at York University, where his dissertation traced Canada’s responses to Afghan displacement from the Cold War to the present, situating refugee policy within changing relations between the state, civil society, and the wider geopolitical order. His current research turns to the afterlife of exceptional resettlement programs, asking how refugee protection encounters questions of settler colonialism, reconciliation, and political belonging in what is now called Canada. He is also a researcher with the Global Migration Institute at Toronto Metropolitan University.

title: Taming the Tyrant: Democracy and Political Accountability in Athens and Today
location: Agincourt, Multipurpose Room, 1st floor
description:
How much power should a single individual have in a democracy? And how might ordinary citizens hold political elites to account? Dr. Ella Street (PhD, Political Theory, University of Toronto) takes us back to classical Athens to explore these enduring questions. Examining the remarkable institutions and cultural practices Athenians developed to keep their leaders in check, she considers what it really means for the demos—the people—to rule supreme.
Despite all that separates ancient and modern democracy, Athens offers surprising lessons for our own moment. As democracies today grapple with powerful individuals—from mayors and heads of state to corporate and technology elites—what might we learn from the Athenians about keeping power in the hands of the people? title: The Information Battle: Elections, Journalism and Misinformation
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall
description:
As elections take place in an increasingly complicated online world, voters are exposed to a huge mix of news, social media posts, AI-generated content, and false information spread by organized groups. New digital technologies have made it easier for people to learn about issues and take part in civic life, but they have also raised concerns about trust, fair elections, and respectful public discussion.
This panel brings together experts in misinformation, journalism, and election administration to explore the challenges and opportunities facing democracy today. How are AI and new technologies changing the way people get information? What do these changes mean for voters, journalists, and election officials? And what can be done to build public trust in elections while helping people stay informed and engaged in public life?

**Monday\, October 19\, 2026 \| 6:30 PM screening**
Looking for something meaningful to do on a Monday evening? Join Nick and fellow movie lovers for a **FREE screening of *The Librarians*** at Hot Docs Ted Rogers Cinema!
This powerful, timely documentary explores the battle over book banning and censorship in the United States. It's a thought-provoking film about freedom of expression, access to information, and the librarians standing up for the right to read.
Come for the documentary, stay for the conversation!

### 🎥 ABOUT THE MOVIE

**The Librarians (2025)**
Directed by Kim A. Snyder, this acclaimed documentary follows librarians on the front lines of an escalating wave of book bans across America.
As books addressing race and LGBTQ+ experiences are challenged and removed from schools and libraries, librarians find themselves facing harassment, threats, and political pressure. The film follows these librarians as they connect the dots between local controversies and wider efforts to restrict access to books and ideas.
It's a compelling look at censorship, democracy, and the people fighting to protect intellectual freedom.

title: David Treuer: The Savage Mind
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
New York Times bestselling author David Treuer shares his groundbreaking, intimate reckoning with the history of North America.
The Savage Mind is a seamless blend of memoir, history and reportage, in which Treuer leverages his unique dual perspective as the son of a Holocaust survivor and the first American Indigenous woman judge in the United States to offer an examination of the distinct nature of North American violence.
In contrast to the frontier thesis of American history, Treuer contends that frontier violence cannot be defined as an external force, but that it has actually entered the culture and taken root in our very selves.
By reckoning with these histories, the book confronts our complicity in either normalizing violence, or blaming it on outside sources, instead of seeing its recurring patterns and contending with its significance.
David Treuer speaks with journalist and author Tanya Talaga about The Savage Mind and shares why he chooses to embrace an ultimately hopefully view of the continent.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
David Treuer
Tanya Talaga
Read more:

The Heartbeat of Wounded Knee

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

description:
The Faculty of Graduate Studies is offering a virtual workshop to support Master’s students preparing applications for the upcoming Tri-Council and Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS) competitions. how to locate the appropriate publisher for your work

how to turn your thesis into a book
the peer review process
sources of funding for scholarly monographs
what to expect of your publisher and what your publisher will expect of you

title: Data Analytics Essentials Learning Circle
location: Palmerston, Meeting Room
description:
Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space!
A
learning circle
is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment.
Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field.
In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to:
transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel
query data from a relational database using SQL
improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau
We will meet weekly,
in-person,
every Tuesday afternoon, September 15 - December 8, 2-3:30 PM (12 sessions).
Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend sessions on a weekly basis.
Learners who complete the course will be able to:
earn a digital badge
download a certificate of completion

title: Python Essentials 1 and 2 Learning Circle
location: York Woods
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Tuesday afternoons from September 22 to December 8, 2-3:30pm. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Learners who successfully complete both courses will earn a digital badge and certificate of completion.
Python Essentials 1
is the first in a 2-course series that teaches computer programming skills including how to design, develop, and improve computer programs using the Python programming language. The course covers essential programming topics such as data types, variables, control flow, functions, and exceptions.
Python Essentials 2
is the second in a 2-course series that will prepare you for the PCAP – Certified Associate in Python Programming certification exam at Pearson VUE. This intermediate-level course covers advanced aspects of Python programming, including modules, packages, exceptions, file processing and object-oriented programming (OOP).

title: ABCD Reads "Salvation of a Saint" by Keigo Higashino
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads "**[Salvation of a Saint](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C2888913)**" by Keigo Higashino.

[RESULTS of the poll for this event]

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"The Devotion of Suspect X was a hit with critics and readers alike. The first major English language publication from the most popular bestselling writer in Japan, it was acclaimed as "stunning," "brilliant," and "ingenious."
Now physics professor Manabu Yukawa—Detective Galileo—returns in a new case of impossible murder, where instincts clash with facts and theory with reality.
Yoshitaka, who was about to leave his marriage and his wife, is poisoned by arsenic-laced coffee and dies. His wife, Ayane, is the logical suspect—except that she was hundreds of miles away when he was murdered. The lead detective, Tokyo Police Detective Kusanagi, is immediately smitten with her and refuses to believe that she could have had anything to do with the crime. His assistant, Kaoru Utsumi, however, is convinced Ayane is guilty. While Utsumi's instincts tell her one thing, the facts of the case are another matter. So she does what her boss has done for years when stymied—she calls upon Professor Manabu Yukawa.
But even the brilliant mind of Dr. Yukawa has trouble with this one, and he must somehow find a way to solve an impossible murder and capture a very real, very deadly murderer.
Salvation of a Saint is Keigo Higashino at his mind-bending best, pitting emotion against fact in a beautifully plotted crime novel filled with twists and reverses that will astonish and surprise even the most attentive and jaded of readers." (from [Macmillan Publishers](https://us.macmillan.com/books/9781250036278/salvationofasaint/))

"When a man is discovered dead by poisoning in his empty home his beautiful wife, Ayane, immediately falls under suspicion. All clues point to Ayane being the logical suspect, but how could she have committed the crime when she was hundreds of miles away?
As Tokyo police detective Kusanagi tries to unpick a seemingly unrelated sequence of events he finds himself falling for Ayane. When his judgement becomes dangerously clouded his assistant must call on an old friend for help; it will take a genius to unravel the most spectacular web of deceit they have ever faced…
SALVATION OF A SAINT is a magnificently complex and page-turning thriller starring international crime fiction’s most enigmatic sleuth.This is essential reading for all fans of exceptional crime fiction." (from [Hachette UK](https://www.hachette.co.uk/titles/keigo-higashino/salvation-of-a-saint/9780349138817/))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Civic Meetup #565: Measuring Main Streets: Data Tools for Transit-Oriented Communities
location: Online: https://link.civictech.ca/zoom / Health Sciences Building
description:
Topic: Measuring Main Streets: Data Tools for Transit-Oriented Communities

Understanding what communities need from housing and transit, and deploying evidence-based responses to those needs is hard. Who's living in housing around transit infrastructure? What amenities are in their neighbourhood, and what's missing? What housing stock exists? How can it be developed further to serve the local community effectively? And of course, how does walkability fit into this whole picture?

To equip community leaders with tools to answer these questions and more, the Canadian Urban Institute (CUI) developed Measuring Main Streets. It's a digital platform bringing together unique neighbourhood-level data on demographics, housing development potential, and community amenities in and around transit station areas.

We'll demo the platform's tools and show how they go beyond traditional transit-oriented development, which tends to focus on density, to make the case for what we call transit-oriented complete communities: places where transit investment also delivers the amenities and housing mix people actually need.

Speakers: Greg Spencer (he/him), Luca Carnegie (he/him)

Greg has over 20 years of experience in urban and economic development policy making and research. He has worked in consulting and academia roles across Canada, the UK, and Ireland helping local communities reach their full potential. He has co-authored high profile reports with leading urban think tanks such as Brookings Metro, The Martin Prosperity Institute, and NESTA. He has also co-authored op-eds in the Globe and Mail, the Toronto Star, and The Guardian. He holds a Ph.D. in Economic Geography and a M.Sc. in Planning from the University of Toronto and a B.A. in Geography from Bishops University.

Luca is a Data Analyst on the Data Analytics Team at the Canadian Urban Institute. After graduating, he dove into urban data science at the CUI to drive evidenced-based, multidisciplinary solutions to urban challenges. He holds a Bachelor of Information in Information Systems from the University of Toronto. In his free time, he loves to watch and act in musical theatre, play music, and test new recipes in his kitchen. This is his second time presenting at Civic Tech and is SO excited to be back!!

title: Jamaluddin Aram: The Blood of Things
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space, North York Central Library (5120 Yonge St), Lower Level
description:
TPL presents Afghan-Canadian writer Jamaluddin Aram in conversation with Dmitri Nasrallah at the North York Central Library's Concourse Event Space.
What does it mean to carry a homeland inside you after it has been lost, not once, but again and again? In his essay collection
The Blood of Things
, Aram turns his attention fully to Afghanistan, its beauty, its suffering, and its complexity. Spanning from the recent fall of Kabul to the early days of Islam, from the myth of the Order of Assassins to the persecution of the country's ethnic Hazara community, Aram weaves personal stories with sweeping historical and political inquiry.
Drawing on his own journey from Afghanistan to Toronto, and his work as associate producer of the Oscar-nominated film
Buzkashi Boys
, Aram brings a novelist's eye for character and an essayist's rigor to bear on questions of identity, belonging, and what remains possible even amid profound loss.
Join Jamaluddin Aram for an intimate evening of readings and conversation on exile, memory, and the enduring pull of home.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:

description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.

title: El día que la IA decidió trabajar en equipo (más JARVIS, menos Skynet)
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
En los últimos meses hemos visto cómo la IA escribe código, genera imágenes o responde preguntas. Pero hay algo mucho más interesante ocurriendo: ¿qué pasa cuando varias IAs empiezan a trabajar juntas como un equipo real?

En esta sesión vamos a llevar esa idea a la práctica montando, desde cero, una factoría de software basada en agentes IA. Cada agente tendrá un rol claro —programador, QA, diseñador, incluso músico— y todos estarán coordinados por un agente orquestador (el “project manager” de toda la vida) que se encargará de repartir tareas, tomar decisiones y mantener el flujo de trabajo.

Lo interesante es que no será teoría: lo veremos en directo. Los agentes se comunicarán entre ellos, pasarán tareas y construirán algo real delante de nosotros. Sin guión y sin red, mostrando cómo funcionan de verdad estos sistemas cuando los pones a trabajar.

Al final tendremos un producto generado por este “enjambre” de agentes, y por el camino habremos visto cómo se diseñan, cómo colaboran y qué problemas reales aparecen cuando intentas llevar esto a la práctica.

title: Embodied Garden: 8-Week Art Therapy Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join Mahja Kabir, an artist and art therapy trainee, for an eight-week closed art therapy group for adults!
Embodied Garden invites participants to slow down, connect with nature, and explore their inner world through creative expression. Each session includes a brief embodiment meditation, gentle check-in, nature-inspired art-making, and optional sharing.
 
Across the eight weeks, the garden becomes both a setting and a metaphor for exploring themes of grounding, growth, movement, boundaries, protection, change, community, and belonging. Each session introduces a distinct theme while contributing to an overarching exploration of embodiment, connection, and our relationship with the natural world.
 
As a closed group, participants are invited to attend all eight sessions. The continuity of the series offers opportunities to build trust, develop connections, and reflect more deeply as the sessions unfold.
 
The group is facilitated by Mahja Kabir, an artist and art therapy trainee who creates gentle, creative spaces that support reflection, care, growth, and connection. Art therapy uses the creative process as a way to explore emotions, experiences, relationships, and self-awareness, with no emphasis on artistic skill or producing a finished artwork.
 
Wednesdays, October 21 through December 9, 10 a.m. to 12 p.m. (eight sessions).
Public $160, TBG Members $120 (plus applicable taxes and fees).

A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

description:
This session will be offered in person at York University’s Markham Campus and is open to students from all York University campuses.
In this week’s session of YU & Balance, we will focus on building realistic self-care and time management habits that fit into student life.
Students will reflect on questions such as:

What motivates me to take care of myself?
What tends to get in the way of self-care?
How can I make time for myself when life gets busy?

Through discussion and reflection, students will explore ways to prioritize their well-being, build self-care into their routines and practice affirmations that support confidence and motivation.
This session is part of a 6-week Recovery College series. For each session attended, participants will receive $5 on their YU-card. description:
