title: Working With Your Go To Emotional State
location: North York Central Library, Room 101
description:
Most of us have a
"go-to emotion."
It is the emotion that shows up automatically when we feel hurt or overwhelmed. That emotion can be
anger, anxiety, depression, guilt, shame, or even emotional numbness.
In this interactive presentation, we will explore how your go-to emotion developed, what purpose it serves, and offer techniques on how to respond from a more measured space.
Join Ann Schnurr, a Registered Psychotherapist with more than 25 years of experience, as she supports adults to understand their go-to emotion for greater emotional resilience, healthier relationships, and a deeper connection with self.
Registration is encouraged
via the library’s website.
Drop-ins welcome until capacity is reached.  For more information contact the Business Science & Technology desk at 416-395-5613

title: Amir Hajian (Awby Knowledge Studio Inc)
location: IdeaLab
description:
Title: The Universal Tango:How AI and Physics are Rewriting the Rules of Scientific Discovery

Abstract: For decades, the relationship between artificial intelligence and physics has been largely one-sided: physicists built the hardware, and AI processed the data. Today, that dynamic has fundamentally shifted into a powerful, bidirectional symbiosis that is redefining both fields. This talk explores the cutting-edge convergence of AI and physics across three critical frontiers.

First, we examine how AI is revolutionizing physical modeling to accelerate traditional simulations by orders of magnitude, effectively breaking the computational bottleneck of classical physics.

Second, we flip the script to explore how physics is rescuing AI, turning hardware "noise" into a computational feature to design ultra-low-energy chips that perform AI inference natively.

Finally, we look to the future of the scientific method itself, the rise of "AI Scientists" and advanced knowledge-work agents. From methods that solve the critical knowledge-management bottlenecks in modern research today, to the more ambitious ones that aim to bring autonomous agents into scientific discovery.

We show through solid examples that we are transitioning from an era where AI merely assists physicists, to an era where AI and physics co-evolve to efficiently unlock the fundamental laws of the universe.
Host: Shantanu Basu

title: Bridging Minds: Menopause, Metabolism and Heart Health: What Changes at Midlife
description:
What happens to your heart and metabolism as you move through menopause? As hormone levels change through the transition, so can the way your body manages cholesterol, blood sugar, fat and other factors that influence long-term heart health.
Join Dr. Iliana Lega for the next Bridging Minds: Health & Science Conversations webinar to understand these changes and what you can do to support your health. Building on last month’s conversation about menopause and brain health, this session broadens the picture to explore heart and metabolic health, practical strategies for prevention, and what current evidence tells us about the role of menopausal hormone therapy.
What to Expect
What changes during menopause:
Understand how the menopause transition can affect cardiovascular risk factors, metabolism, body composition and weight.
What you can do:
Explore practical lifestyle and preventive strategies to support heart and metabolic health during midlife.
The role of hormone therapy:
Learn what current evidence tells us about menopausal hormone therapy and cardiovascular and metabolic health.
About the Presenter
Dr. Iliana Lega is a staff endocrinologist at Women’s College Hospital, and a scientist at the Women’s College Hospital Research and Innovation Institute. Dr. Lega’s clinical interests lie in the area of diabetes, as well as reproductive endocrinology, including Premature Ovarian Insufficiency (POI), Turner syndrome, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), and Menopause.
About the Series
Bridging Minds: Health & Science Conversations is a partnership between the Toronto Public Library and Women’s College Hospital. Through monthly discussions led by experts from across different clinical areas and scientific disciplines, this series provides attendees with the opportunity to engage directly with our topics and speakers and empowers communities to navigate health and science topics confidently, inspiring a future of informed decision-making.
Learn more:

title: New Sounds, New Space Report Launch + Wavelength Documentary Premiere
location: St. Anne's Parish Hall,651 Dufferin St, Toronto, ON M6K 2B2, Canada
description:
Presented with Sonic Boom


October 21, 2026
Wavelength @ St. Anne’s

651 Dufferin St.

6PM

Free - RSVP at http://bit.ly/NSNSwl


You are invited to join Wavelength for an evening of original content! Local music lovers will enjoy this free presentation, panel, and screening plus a networking session soundtracked by DJ Uncle Chayne.


Be the first to view Wavelength: 25 Years of Music & Community, a short documentary written and directed by Ian Daffern (Idfactory) telling the story of Toronto’s unique artist-run concert series and non-profit organization. A who’s who of Canadian music, this project was scored and mixed by Justin Small (Do Make Say Think, BODY///GRAVE) and music supervised by Babs V. Westerholm (Cue Queens) and features interviews with Melissa Auf der Maur (Hole, Smashing Pumpkins), Emilie Hanskamp, pHoenix Pagliacci, Charles Spearin (Broken Social Scene, Do Make Say Think), and Wavelength’s Jonathan Bunce (AKA Jonny Dovercourt). Additional music by Burs, Luge, MOONBEAN, Orbital Ensemble, Paul Chin, Pony Da Look, Rich Aucoin, Sook-Yin Lee and more.


A follow up to 2023’s acclaimed Reimagining Music Venues Study, the launch of the “New Sounds, New Space” report explores different pathways for establishing community hubs for Toronto’s grassroots music community. With positive case studies on Hugh’s Room Live, It’s Ok* Studios, Small World Music and Primal Note Studios, the report shines light on Toronto’s post-COVID music venue landscape while pointing the way forward for imaginative new spaces. Funded by Canada Council for the Arts “Seed” grant!


Join in on the conversation that shapes Toronto’s music culture from the ground up.

Join us for our October Python Toronto meetup on **Wednesday, October 21st**, hosted at [The Adaptavist Group](https://www.adaptavist.com/) office at **43 Front St. East**, Toronto.

If you are interested in giving a talk, we'd love to have you! Please fill out this form: [Submit a Python Toronto talk](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfpNKB0Sbs893xp72M4TxmYGrTyLm4Nh1SSXnCqChP9mx6_9A/viewform?usp=header)! Talks are typically 5 - 10 minutes, or up to 20 minutes for longer presentations. Topics can cover anything interesting to the Python community, from Python libraries and developer tools to AI, data science, research, or projects you've been working on.

The Python meetup is a casual, community-oriented meetup hosted by companies that use Python in Toronto. Talks are short, informal, and sometimes ad-hoc.

Space is limited! Register now to hold your spot!

When/Where

* **When:** October 21, 2026, 6pm – 8pm. Doors open at 5:30, talks start around 6.
* Come early to enjoy **snacks** and **drinks** provided.
* **Address**: [The Adaptavist Group](https://www.adaptavist.com/) \- 43 Front St\. East\, Toronto\, ON\.

**Code of Conduct**
Python Toronto is dedicated to providing a welcoming, harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of gender, gender identity and expression, age, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion (or lack thereof), or technology choices. We do not tolerate harassment of any form. Sexual language and imagery is not appropriate for this venue, including talks, workshops, parties, Twitter and other online media. Meetup participants violating these rules may be sanctioned or expelled from the meetup (without a refund where applicable) at the discretion of the meetup organizers. Please email elaine@eswong.ca to report any issues.

title: Friendships and other Complexities ft. Roger Berkowitz
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
This evening’s theme explores the challenge of staying in dialogue and connection across our differences through Hannah Arendt’s friendships.
Make the most of your
Connect IRL
experience by coming before or staying after the featured event. Grab a drink or snack at the bar. Sign up for
The Friendship Test Workshop
(see registration below) or try out one of the engagement activities available, including tonight’s
Conversation Station: The Kitchen Table
, where you can take a moment or two to connect with a stranger to reflect on the rewards and challenges of friendship.
*****
Join us at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon
for
Friendships and other Complexities
with political theorist Roger Berkowitz in conversation with Sanjay Ruparelia.
This one is about the harder kind of connection: staying in relationships with people you disagree with. We'll consider friendship not as a private comfort but as political work; the daily, unglamorous business of talking with people whose views unsettle us and whose reasoning we may never fully understand. Expect to be asked what you're willing to hold open, and to talk it through with people who won't necessarily see it your way.
What can Hannah Arendt's friendships — including with people whose politics she found troubling — teach us about sustaining democracy today? If our current political crisis is, at its root, a crisis of friendship, what has eroded our capacity to stay in dialogue across difference? And in an age of mass loneliness and ideological certainty, what would it mean to treat friendship, rather than consensus or moral purity, as the foundation of democratic life?
Berkowitz is founder and academic director of the Hannah Arendt Center for Politics and Humanities at Bard College. In A World We Share: Hannah Arendt and the Power of Friendship in a Broken World, he rethinks politics through Arendt's own life — a Jewish woman who escaped Nazi Germany, lived as an exile in Paris and then New York, and became a bold critic of popular ideas after World War II. People who knew her said she had a special talent for making friends. Berkowitz argues that a politics built solely on being right becomes cruel, coercive and ultimately anti-political.
Come ready to disagree agreeably.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Roger Berkowitz
Sanjay Ruparelia
Read more:
World We Share : Hannah Arendt and the Power of Friendship in A Broken World
***
Sign up for The Friendship Test Workshop
|
5:30 - 6:30 pm
The Kitchen Table |
5:30–6:30 pm & 8:00 – 9:00 pm
Grab a seat and dig into the questions we rarely ask out loud: How has your definition of friendship changed? Can you stay close to someone you disagree with? What makes a friendship last? Inspired by Berkowitz's argument that friendship — not agreement — is the glue of a healthy society, this café is a space to reflect on your own circle with the strangers sitting next to you.
Connect IRL
is not your average series of events, workshops and activities, but a real chance to connect with other Torontonians in meaningful and sometimes unexpected ways. Through conversation stations meant to spark one-on-one conversations, or hands-on engagement activities and workshops before the featured event, participants can explore the value of connection and community.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: Centre for Feminist Research Graduate Student Conference: “Assemblia”
location: 519 Kaneff Tower
description:
Date: October 22, 2026
Time: 10:00 AM–4:00 PM
Location: York University, Keele Campus
The Centre for Feminist Research is pleased to announce that we are accepting submissions for our upcoming conference, ASSEMBLIA, taking place on October 22, 2026.
This is the inaugural conference in what we hope will become an annual event organized by graduate students and members of the CFR. It provides an interdisciplinary forum for emerging and independent artists and scholars by bringing together studio practice, criticism and theory, gender studies, and art history.
We welcome academic articles, poetry, short fiction, artworks, and essays. Any questions can be directed towards the Assemblia Graduate Student Leadership Team (Julia and Ame) at CFRfeministfestival@gmail.com
The conference is free and open to graduate students, independent scholars, artists, and interdisciplinary practitioners. Any questions can be directed towards the Assemblia Graduate Student Leadership Team (Julia and Ame) at CFRfeministfestival@gmail.com
Our Objective
Assemblia is organized through a collaborative, non-hierarchical structure grounded in accessibility, shared decision-making, and collective accountability.
Assemblia approaches feminism as a lived practice—often present even when it is not named. Across cultures and histories, feminist resistance has been misrecognized as hysteria, sanctity, deviance, or danger. Assemblia brings together people interested in attending to the language of feminism as acts of care, survival, and uprising.
 
Click HERE  ( https://www.yorku.ca/cfr/cfr-feminist-festival-call-for-volunteers/ )to apply to be a volunteer.
Click HERE  ( https://www.yorku.ca/cfr/assemblia2026-information-submission-guidelines/ )to access the Call for Papers

title: In-Depth Intro to Woodworking Oct 22 [Thursdays - 6 week Intensive]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
Woodworking at TTLMakerspace

 
 Suitable for beginners, this woodworking course is designed to teach you all that you need to get started in woodworking by learning both traditional, and modern techniques.

 Students will learn valuable hands-on skills working on instructor-lead projects using both hand and power tools.

 Projects are chosen to provide skills development in a natural progression from familiarity with the unique characteristics of wood, to basic essential techniques, to some more advanced topics.

 Materials and equipment for all projects are provided with the course. 

 

 Schedule : 

 Six three-hour weekly classes, Thursdays 10am to 1pm. 

 Outcomes : 

 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 

 
- A complete understanding of the nature and properties of wood 

- Proficiency with traditional woodworking techniques

- Comfort working with chisels, planes, saws

- Proficiency with wood milling techniques

- Comfort with safe operation of power tools

- Familiarity with power planing, joiner, drill press, router and table saw 

- Dressing and laminating wood 

- Experience following project plans 

- Familiarity with joinery 

- Wood finishing, various treatments 

 
  Following this course, you'll be certified to use the woodshop. And you'll be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing knowledge on our Discord community.

 Certifications for all courses are valid for one year from the time that they are issued, and can be renewed at no cost with your active monthly membership within 3 months of their expiry. Certification renewal requires booking with an instructor, is conducted at the makerspace, and helps you keep your skills current. 

Useful for: furniture, cabinets, organisers, cutting-boards 
 
 
 
 Want to get notified next time classes are posted? 

 Join our mailing list!

The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. title: Oct 22 - Advances in AI at Virginia Tech
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from AI researchers at Virginia Tech!

**Date, Time and Location**

Oct 22, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
**[Online. Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/advances-in-ai-at-virginia-tech-october-22-2026)**

**Multi-Agent Communication: A framework, diagnostic and mechanistic perspective**

Multi-agent LLM systems are increasingly used for collaborative reasoning, debate, and consensus, yet their communication dynamics remain poorly understood. This talk presents a framework for studying multi-agent communication through diagnostic and mechanistic perspectives.

I will discuss CONSENSAGENT, which improves consensus by mitigating sycophancy, alongside our diagnostic work on communication patterns and failure modes in real-world multi-agent debates. I will then present ongoing work that moves toward a mechanistic understanding of how these interaction patterns arise internally, with the broader goal of making multi-agent systems more interpretable, reliable, and controllable.

*About the Speaker*

[Priya Pitre](https://www.linkedin.com/in/priya-p-a31360117/) I am an Ph.D student in the Computer Science Department at Virginia Tech (VT), co-advised by Dr. Xuan Wang and Dr. Naren Ramakrishnan.

**Exposing and Improving Fine-Grained Visual Grounding Abilities of Lightweight Multimodal LLMs**

Lightweight multimodal LLMs can localize whole objects effectively, yet often struggle when a query targets a small object part or fine-grained visual detail. This talk presents a reasoning-guided framework that teaches compact models to ground parts through an explicit coarse-to-fine process: first locating the parent object, then identifying the requested part.

A part-aware reinforcement-learning objective provides stage-wise rewards for object accuracy, part containment, and the consistency of the model’s self-critique. Using these techniques, a compact 4B-parameter model achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot part grounding while preserving its object-level performance.

These advances can be used to enable lightweight MLLMs to support detail-oriented tasks in biology and robotics.

*About the Speaker*

[Kazi Mehrab ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ksmehrab/)I a CS PhD candidate at Virginia Tech, where I currently focus on multimodal LLMs and computer vision tasks, including visual perception, reasoning and grounding.

**Understanding Visual Generative Models for Precise Control**

Despite remarkable progress in image and video generation, translating user intent into precise and consistent visual outputs remains a challenge. This talk explores how understanding the representations within generative models can enable finer control over what they create.

It connects semantic image editing with compositional generation, examining how visual concepts can be isolated, manipulated, and combined while preserving their identity and surrounding content. Building on these insights, structured visual inputs provide a way to express complex intent through subject references, poses, and spatial layouts.

The discussion then extends from images to video, where representations must evolve to preserve scene continuity while accommodating motion and change. Together, these directions establish a unified perspective on how visual representations can support controllable editing, composition, and coherent generation across space and time.

*About the Speaker*

[Yusuf Dalva](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yusuf-dalva/) is a Ph.D. candidate at Virginia Tech, advised by Pinar Yanardag and affiliated with the Sanghani Center for Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics.

title: Common Hour – Tango Concert
location: Tribute Communities Recital Hall @ Accolade East Building 83 York Boulevard, Toronto
description:
Join us for a free noon-hour concert featuring Solidaridad Tango ( https://solidaridadtango.ca/ ), an acclaimed ensemble dedicated to celebrating the rich heritage and vibrant energy of tango.
Led by Sri Lankan-Canadian violinist and composer Aparna Halpé, the group brings together world-class international artistry with Belgian bandoneónist Eva Wolff and master double bassist Ignacio Varchausky. Don’t miss this midday showcase of passion, community, and extraordinary musical tradition!
Date: Thursday, October 22
Time: 12:30 – 1:30 p.m.
Location: Tribute Communities Recital Hall ( https://www.google.ca/maps/place/83+York+Blvd,+North+York,+ON+M7A+2C5/@43.7728892,-79.4999096,560m/data=!3m2!1e3!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x882b2e24bf73dcab:0xd9125a796619a45!8m2!3d43.7728892!4d-79.4999096!16s%2Fg%2F1tvm3d63?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDkyMC4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D )
FREE Admission
Eva Wolff, Bandoneon
Eva Wolff ( https://solidaridadtango.ca/tfts-eva-wolff ) was born in Ghent, Belgium in 1978. At the age of 15, she started studying bandoneón at Codarts, the Rotterdam Conservatory, under the guidance of Leo Vervelde. She graduated in 2001. In the same year she won a scholarship granted by the Netherlands, which permitted her to live and study for one year in Buenos Aires as a student at the Orquesta Escuela de Tango Emilio Balcarce directed by Emilio Balcarce himself.
Ignacio Varchausky, Double Bass
Bassist Ignacio Varchausk ( https://www.ignaciovarchausky.com/ )y is the creator and artistic director of the Orquesta Escuela de Tango Emilio Balcarce which was founded in 2000 and is funded by the Ministry of Culture of Buenos Aires. For over 25 years, Varchausky has taught and lectured worldwide, including at the Teatro Colón in Buenos Aires, the Edgar Varese Conservatoire in Gennevilliers, the Sydney Conservatorium of Music, CODARTS University of the Arts in Rotterdam, University of London Americas Society in New York, Ibero-American Institute in Berlin, and Reed College in Portland.
Aparna Halpé, Violin, Viola, Cello
Aparna Halpé ( https://solidaridadtango.ca/tfts-aparna-halpe ) is a Sri Lankan-Canadian tango violinist, arranger, and composer, based in Toronto. She holds Licentiates of the Guildhall School of Music and the Royal Schools of Music, UK. In 2021, Aparna founded the all-women, diversity-focused tango ensemble, Solidaridad Tango, creating a tango practice grounded in principles of diversity, equity, and inclusion that foregrounds the careers of immigrant women musicians in tango. In 2025, she founded the free community music-making project, the Toronto Tango Community Orchestra, which invites musicians of all ages and abilities to experience the joy of learning tango while building stronger community relationships. In 2026, under Aparna’s direction, the TTCO was invited by RED Por La Identidad Canada to headline the fundraising event for the Abuelas de Plaza de Mayo which commemorated the victims of Argentina’s 1976 coup.

title: Tubman Talks with Dr. Marie Laure Belomo Onguene: Peak Technology, Banking and Gender Economic Inclusion in Africa
location: Zoom: https://yorku.zoom.us/meeting/register/K-bk-9K5Qm-JZMX3T3pK8g
description:
Tubman Talks with Dr. Marie Laure Belomo Onguene: Peak Technology, Banking and Gender Economic Inclusion in Africa
Date: Thursday, October 22, 2026
Time: 2:00pm – 3:30pm EDT
Location: Zoom
Register Here: https://yorku.zoom.us/meeting/register/K-bk-9K5Qm-JZMX3T3pK8g
Title: Peak Technology, Banking and Gender Economic Inclusion in Africa
Abstract
The focus of the study is how mobile money moderates the effect of peak technology on gender economic inclusion in Africa, with thresholds of mobile money at which the effect
of peak technology on gender economic inclusion is mitigated, as well as evidence of positive synergies between digital finance and frontier technologies. Using a panel dataset of 31 African countries over the period 2010-2023, and drawing on fixed-effects models, Driscoll–Kraay robust estimations, Lewbel (2012) instrumental variable approaches, and quantile regressions, the study produces the following key findings. First, the baseline linear estimates indicate that frontier technology readiness (FRTI) is, on average, positively and significantly associated with the share of women in the labor force. Second, interactive and instrumental variable specifications reveal a fundamental structural heterogeneity: when mobile money and digital payment services are absent, the marginal effect of FRTI on women’s economic inclusion turns negative or insignificant. Third, threshold analysis identifies specific levels of financial digitalization beyond which the adverse effect of frontier technologies is fully mitigated or reversed into a positive synergy. These thresholds vary across specifications (ranging from approximately 0.53 to 1.65 on the digital finance scales) but consistently confirm a non-linear complementarity between technological capability and digital financial inclusion. Fourth, quantile regression results establish that the inclusive effect of technology is most pronounced at the upper end of the distribution of female labor force participation. Policy implications are discussed.

Bio
Marie Laure BELOMO ONGUENE is a lecturer in the Faculty of Economics and Management at the University of Yaoundé 2 Soa. She holds a Ph.D. from the University of Dschang in Cameroon and served as a postdoctoral researcher in the Open AIR program at the Center for Law, Technology, and Society at the University of Ottawa. In addition, she serves as a visiting researcher in the Department of Economics at York University in Canada under the supervision of Pralewa Yinka Olawoye. Between May 2023 and August 2023, she received a research mobility grant from the Observatory of the Economic Francophonie at the University of Lomé in Togo. Her research focuses on the socioeconomic challenges that emigration poses to migrants’ countries of origin. She is particularly interested in economic complexity, women’s political empowerment, and food security.

 Outcomes : 
 
 
 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 
 
 
- 
 A complete understanding of the steps needed to go from concept to completed part 

- 
 Familiarity with the properties of a variety of hardwood materials 

- 
 Experience and comprehension of the most important principles of CAD modelling 

- 
 Selecting and programming the most commonly used tools 

- 
 Full understanding of the most common machining operations 

- 
 Experience creating tool paths with CAM software 

- 
 Setting up a CNC mill and performing operations 

- 
 Machine maintenance and Safety 

 
 
 Following this course, you’ll be certified to use desktop mills, and book time with the industrial mill at TTLMakerspace (with your membership). You will also be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing CNC knowledge on our Discord community.

title: From Ancient Americas to Ancestral Abiayala
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:
From Ancient Americas to Ancestral Abiayala            
                                    
                                
                        
                                                
                                                        Get Tickets                        
                                            
                
                    
    



	

    
         
    




	


			

    
        
             
                
                    Thursday October 22, 2026
6:00 pm – 8:00 pm
 
The Diane Wolfe Lecture 
Speaker: Juliana Ramírez Herrera, Ph.D., Assistant Professor of Indigenous Art and Archaeology of the Ancestral Americas and of Colonial Latin American Art, University of California, Berkeley 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    Join Dr. Juliana Ramírez Herrera, curator of the Gardiner Museum’s Ancestral Abiayala Gallery—formerly Ancient Americas—for a conversation on repatriation, broadly understood, and how it shaped her vision for the renovated space. 
Drawing on other threads of her research, Dr. Ramírez Herrera will situate Ancestral Abiayala within larger conversations about the mobility of belongings, violent and otherwise, and what it might mean to care for them responsibly in museum practice and scholarly writing. 
The talk offers a behind-the-scenes look at what went into developing the Ancestral Abiayala Gallery, connecting its questions to broader intellectual debates in the field.

                    About the Speaker
                    
                
                
                    Dr. Juliana Ramírez Herrera
                    
                
                
                    Dr. Juliana Ramírez Herrera is Assistant Professor of Indigenous Art and Archaeology of the Ancestral Americas and of Colonial Latin American Art at the University of California, Berkeley. She specializes in the so-called small-scale societies of pre-Conquest and early colonial Panama, Colombia, the Caribbean, and Amazonia. Before joining UC Berkeley, she was a SSHRC Postdoctoral Fellow at the University of Toronto and the Gardiner Museum of Ceramic Art, where she collaborated with curators Dr. Sequoia Miller, Dr. Karine Tsoumis, and Franchesca Hebert-Spence on the renovation of the Museum’s ground floor. She earned her PhD from Harvard University and her MA from the University of Toronto.

title: Club de lecture théâtre avec le Théâtre français de Toronto
location: Toronto Reference Library, Founders' Room (rez-de-chaussée)
description:
La Bibliothèque publique de Toronto et le
Théâtre français de Toronto
s'associent pour créer un club de lecture théâtre. Ce rendez-vous mensuel est l'occasion de discuter et d'explorer des scènes mythiques ayant marqué le monde du théâtre. Avec
Georges Som
, médiateur culturel, nous essayerons de comprendre les enjeux de ces scènes, de découvrir leurs sens et de partager nos sentiments sur leurs auteurs et autrices. Chacun est le bienvenu au club, qu'il soit néophyte ou amateur de théâtre confirmé. Les seuls prérequis pour participer sont la curiosité et le plaisir d'échanger autour du théâtre !
Au mois d'octobre, nous allons discuter un extrait de la pièce
Rhinocéros
de Eugène Ionesco.  Le sublime se confond avec le ridicule dans ce commentaire féroce sur la condition humaine, un incontournable de tout cours de théâtre et du théâtre du 20e siècle. Une petite ville est assiégée par un citoyen rugissant qui se transforme en rhinocéros et se met à piétiner l'ordre social. À mesure que d'autres citoyens se transforment en rhinocéros, le piétinement devient écrasant, et de plus en plus de citoyens deviennent des rhinocéros. Un seul homme sain d'esprit, Bérenger, reste incapable de changer de forme et d'identité.
Rhinocéros

# 👻 Ghost Tour: The Exhibition Grounds 🎡

### Toronto's Haunted Fairgrounds, Dark History & One Building I Don't Like Being Near

The Exhibition Grounds have spent more than a century hosting crowds, celebrations, soldiers, shows, and some of Toronto's biggest events.
But underneath all that history is a darker side.

The Exhibition Grounds are said to be **one of the most haunted places in Toronto** — and I'll be honest: **this is the one place on my ghost walks that genuinely scares me.**

There's something about the atmosphere here.
Some buildings have an energy that feels different. And when you know what happened in them, it's hard not to look at them a little differently.

On this evening ghost walk, we'll explore the grounds and hear stories of **soldiers, settlers, performers, animals, tragedies, and people who may never have completely left.**

This isn't just about trying to scare you.
It's about discovering the strange history hiding underneath one of Toronto's most familiar landmarks.

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 👻 What We'll Explore

We'll begin outside **Medieval Times** and make our way across the Exhibition Grounds toward the Princes' Gates.
Along the way, we'll hear stories connected to:

* 🏚️ **The General Service Building**
* 💀 **The Stanley Barracks** — the building that genuinely creeps me out
* 🐎 **The Horse Palace**
* 🏠 **Scadding Cabin**
* 👻 Other strange stories, unexplained encounters, and haunted corners of the grounds

We'll finish at the **Princes' Gates**.
We'll keep a steady walking pace and **will not be entering any of the buildings**.

***

## 🕯️ Why This One Is Different

I've done a lot of ghost walks around Toronto.
**This is the one that actually makes me uncomfortable.**
Maybe it's the history. Maybe it's the buildings. Maybe it's simply knowing what happened here and then standing there after dark.

Whatever it is, the Exhibition Grounds have always felt different to me.

So come prepared for some genuinely creepy stories — and maybe a few moments where we all wonder whether we should really be standing there. 👻

***

## 🧢 Meetup Details

📍 **Meetup Location:** In front of **Medieval Times**
🫎 **Look for me in my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time:** **6:30 PM sharp**
I will only wait **5 minutes**.
**Early is on time. On time is late.**
🚶‍♂️ **Pace:** Steady walking pace
🏁 **End Point:** **Princes' Gates**

***

## 🎟️ Meetup Fee

**$10 cash in person or e-transfer**
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**
This is a **curated ghost-walking experience**, rather than one of our regular social walks. The route, stories, and history have been researched and brought together specifically for this experience.
The fee helps support the time and work that goes into creating these walks.

***

## 🎒 What to Bring

👟 Comfortable walking shoes
🧥 Weather-appropriate clothing
💧 Water
📱 Your phone for photos
And maybe… don't wander off by yourself. 👻

***

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This experience is great for:

* 👻 People who love ghost stories
* 🏙️ Anyone fascinated by Toronto's darker history
* 🕯️ Fans of the strange and unexplained
* 🎡 People who want to see the Exhibition Grounds differently
* 🚶 Anyone looking for something unusual to do on an evening out
* 😈 People who like being scared — at least a little

You don't have to believe in ghosts.
**You just have to be willing to walk into the dark with us.**

***

**REMEMBER:** You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**

Questions? Post on the event wall or email:
📧 **torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com**

**Come for the history.**
**Stay for the ghost stories.**
**And try not to look too closely at the buildings.** 👻

title: From Portfolio to Book
description:
Join us for an online special career series with the
2026 Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence
, Elly MacKay! In this series, Elly will share insights into building a career in children’s book illustration, covering topics such as the journey to working as an illustrator, an overview of classic children’s books, portfolios, and colour. Details about each session follow:
Thursday, October 8, 7pm:
Becoming an Illustrator
Elly MacKay shares her early and current work, her career path, and her process for creating miniature 3D worlds. Her talk also covers developing your style, illustration trends, and how to stand out.
Thursday, October 15, 7pm: Looking at Picture Books
Elly MacKay gives an overview of famous picture books, the various styles, what works, and how they’ve changed over the years. She looks at cover design, structure, page turns, and how visual storytelling and words work together.
Thursday, October 22, 7pm: From Portfolio to Book
Elly MacKay discusses portfolios and what to include, as well as working with agents and publishers. She also looks at what goes into creating your first picture book.
Thursday, October 29, 7pm: Colour and Atmosphere
Elly MacKay considers colour in picture books—how it can be used to strengthen a message, or to alter the mood. She looks at how illustrators have used colour in unconventional ways in their books.
Workshops will be recorded and available for replay through Zoom until October 31, 2026.
About Elly MacKay
Elly MacKay is a children’s book author and illustrator and a paper artist. She studied printmaking and illustration at NSCAD University in Halifax and University of Canterbury in Christchurch. Elly creates miniature worlds with drawing, painting and cutting, and photographs them for illustrations in children’s books. She has more than 20 books published in Canada and the US, including The Enchanted Symphony by Julie Andrews and Emma Walton Hamilton, I Am a Meadow Mermaid and The Secret Fawn by Kallie George. Elly is both author and illustrator of Frostfire, In the Clouds and Red Sky at Night and others. She lives with her family in Owen Sound, Ontario.
About the Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence Program
The
Illustrator in Residence
program honours the memory of illustrator Joanne Fitzgerald (1956-2011), and is a joint program of IBBY Canada, Toronto Public Library, and the Young Family.

title: Waste Audit Training Course
location: Room N004 Schulich School of Business Building (Basement Floor)
description:
The contemporary discourse around environmental sustainability is shifting from linear extraction models to a Circular Economy. With global waste expected to rise sharply by 2050, managing material flows is essential for resource conservation and climate mitigation. Stricter regulations are driving this change, including Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) frameworks and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) mandates. Waste is no longer just an operational byproduct. It is a measurable source of Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions and a financial risk for organizations that fail to adapt. Many institutions have set “Net-Zero” targets, but they often lack the methods to measure their output accurately. This course fills that gap by teaching participants to quantify and characterize waste streams. The curriculum relies on data-driven auditing rather than estimates or guesswork. This approach gives participants the technical skills to spot inefficiencies, optimize procurement, ensure compliance, and reduce reliance on landfills.
A microcredit certificate will be issued to all participants from CIFAL York-UNITAR.
Instructor: Dr. Calvin Lakhan ( https://www.linkedin.com/in/calvin-lakhan-ph-d-56329224/ ), Director, Circular Innovation Hub, York University
More Information ( https://www.yorku.ca/cifal/waste-audit/ )
Registration link ( https://www.eventbrite.com/e/2002212106308?aff=oddtdtcreator )

title: ¿Y si tu próximo agente fuera una Logic App? Conversacional, autónomo y MCP Serv
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
Cuando pensamos en construir agentes de IA, pensamos en frameworks, SDKs y todo el boilerplate que hay que montar antes de que el agente haga algo útil. Pero hay otro camino: Logic Apps ha incorporado el agent loop a su motor de workflows, ahora todo lo que ya tenía (conectores, ejecución durable, retries, monitorización, managed identities) se convierte en infraestructura de agentes que te viene dada.

En esta sesión, creamos en directo sobre un mismo escenario, un asistente de soporte interno, para poder compararlas bien: Parte 1, el agente conversacional. Creamos el agente desde el designer, le conectamos el modelo y le damos sus primeras tools usando conectores. Vemos cómo se depura de verdad: run history, transcripción del chat, y qué entra y sale del modelo en cada vuelta del loop. Y resolvemos el problema que casi nadie cuenta: el contexto de usuario.

Con autorización on-behalf-of, las tools dejan de ejecutarse con una cuenta de servicio y pasan a actuar con la identidad del usuario que está chateando: si el agente manda un correo, sale de tu buzón. Desplegamos el agente en Microsoft Teams. Parte 2, el agente autónomo.

Mismo escenario, pero sin nadie al otro lado: un trigger de evento arranca el workflow, el agente clasifica, decide y ejecuta por su cuenta. Vemos dónde colocar las agent actions dentro de un workflow normal, cómo combinar varias, y qué pasa con las ejecuciones de larga duración, los errores y la gobernanza cuando no hay un humano mirando.

Parte 3, la Logic App como MCP Server. Le damos la vuelta a la tortilla: en lugar de que el agente viva en Logic Apps, exponemos nuestros workflows como tools MCP para que los consuma cualquier agente externo, desde VS Code hasta el agente que tú quieras. Qué requisitos tiene que cumplir un workflow para ser una tool, cómo se gestionan las API keys y cómo montar varios MCP Servers en una misma Logic App.

Además, hablaremos sobre decisiones de arquitectura: Consumption con modelo gestionado por Microsoft o Standard trayendo tu propio modelo de Foundry, con sus diferencias en redes, autenticación, billing y desarrollo local. Si vienes del mundo pro-code, esta sesión te va a sorprender: no se trata de elegir entre código o designer, sino de saber cuándo el motor de Logic Apps te ahorra construir la mitad de tu plataforma de agentes.

Key Takeaways: Cómo construir agentes conversacionales y autónomos con el agent loop de Logic Apps, y en qué se diferencian Cómo ejecutar tools con la identidad real del usuario mediante autorización on-behalf-of Cómo desplegar tu agente en Microsoft Teams para que hable donde ya están tus usuarios Cómo exponer workflows como MCP Servers remotos consumibles desde cualquier agente o cliente MCP Consumption o Standard: qué SKU elegir según modelo, redes, billing y compliance.

title: Google AI Essentials: In Person Learning Circle
location: Northern District
description:
Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization.
This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz.
By completing the specialization,
you will learn:
How AI works
How to write effective prompts
How to use generative AI tools responsibly
How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm
How to stay up to date with AI news
After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions.

title: Archaeoastronomy: Stonehenge and All That
location: Yorkville
description:
Join us at the Yorkville Library for an Archaeoastronomy Lecture. Archaeoastronomy
is the interdisciplinary study of how people in the past have understood the phenomena in the sky, how they used these phenomena, and what role the sky played in their cultures.  Today, astronomy is considered to mean the scientific study of the universe, but it  continues to connect, in so many  other intriguing ways, with every aspect of cultures, including myth, religion, and the arts.

title: New Date Fall Lighted Walking Trail Discounted + Dinner (Milton)
description:
Experience Toronto
Note: The 10% off on the site may expire at any time.

On **Friday October 23rd,** **join us for Pumpkins After Dark in Milton.** Pumpkins After Dark **is Canada's award-winning outdoor Halloween event -** a family-friendly walk-through experience featuring more than 10,000 hand-carved jack-o'-lanterns lighting up trails every fall. This event is available in Canada, the United States, and Ireland. Each season, their team of artists hand-carves thousands of pumpkins, builds themed scenes - from dinosaurs and dragons to pop-culture icons - and lights a glowing trail to wander together. No jump scares. Just craft, wonder, and the warm glow of a thousand pumpkins. We will be seeing the **Show with the Maze** only. **Purchase your ticket for Pumpkins After Dark Show with the Maze on Friday October 23rd at 7:30pm.**

**World Tour**
Travel the world through the eyes of Halloween with displays organized by continent. Pick up a passport and collect a stamp or letter in each continent to spell a word.

**Brand New Show**
Discover dancing leprechauns, a larger-than-life Eiffel Tower, the Colosseum and Greek mythology, a moving windmill and Holland flower field, Mount Scaremore, and a moving aquarium.

**Pumpkinhead Ed Scavenger Hunt**
Pumpkinhead Ed has escaped and is hiding on the grounds. Find Ed, snap a photo, and tag @findpumpkinheaded for your chance to win a grand prize.

**Interactive Fun**
Explore word searches, puzzles, pumpkin toss games, a trick-or-treat area, and stop by the Witches’ Brew to collect your slime bottle courtesy of The Lab.

title: One Last Backcountry Weekend in Frontenac
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/weekend-in-frontenac)**

**Fall (aka shoulder season) camping brings the serene beauty of the backcountry, without the crowds and bugs.**

At this time of year, Frontenac will be less busy and the trail into Big Clear Lake belongs mostly to us. It's a 9km hike to reach the site, working through root tangled trails and stretches of open granite typical of this stretch of the Canadian Shield. Only the most stubborn leaves will remain on the trees and you’ll enjoy long sightlines through bare branches where the canopy used to be. The pace is steady and moderate the whole way in, never technical but never quite letting up either.

We set up camp on the shore of Big Clear Lake as the light starts to drop, we get a fire going, and cook dinner together. Late October nights out here are serene, with a sky full of stars over the lake.

In the morning, we’ll take our time over breakfast before packing up and heading out along the other side of Big Salmon Lake: a different stretch of trail from the one we hiked in on, with its own look at the park before we're back where we started.

By the time we're back at the cars, you'll have had that sweet final night of the year in the backcountry.

What's included

* Professional & certified guides
* ‍All camp meals, cooking equipment and mess kits
* ‍Tents

Sleeping bags and sleep pads can be rented from WU for a small fee.

**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com

**Highlights**
**Last Trip of the Season:** The final overnight on the calendar before WU's backcountry program pauses for winter
**Shoulder Season Solitude**: Long, quiet stretches of trail, with the lake mostly to yourselves.
**A Clear Night Sky:** Bare branches and dry autumn air make for some of the best stargazing conditions of the year at the campsite.

**Event cost: $265+HST. $70 optional transport also available. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/weekend-in-frontenac)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: 🍂 Fall Walk: Rouge National Urban Park and Picnic🌳
description:
Try New Things in Toronto!
# 🍂🌳 Fall Walk: Rouge National Urban Park 🌳🍁

### A Real Hike, Beautiful Fall Colours & a Picnic Together

Want to get out of the city without actually leaving Toronto?

**Rouge National Urban Park** is Canada's only urban national park — and one of the most popular hikes we do.
Once you get onto the trail, it can be hard to believe you're still in Toronto. Forest paths, rolling hills, changing leaves, and quiet stretches of wilderness make this feel much more like a trip outside the city than a walk through it.
And fall is one of the best times to experience it.

This is **a real hike**, though. There are some hills and ups and downs, so it isn't the best choice if you're looking for an easy, flat walk.
But if you're up for the challenge, there's something satisfying about reaching the end knowing you did it together.
And then we'll have a picnic. 🧺

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 🥾 What We'll Do

We'll meet at **Don Mills Station** and take the 85C bus together toward Rouge National Urban Park.
Once we arrive, we'll begin our hike through the park.
Along the way we'll:

* Hike through forest and open spaces 🌳
* Enjoy the fall colours 🍂
* Navigate the hills and changing terrain
* Take in some beautiful views
* Stop for a short break along the route
* Finish at the Park's Welcome Centre
* Have a **30–40 minute group picnic** afterward 🧺

The hike takes approximately **2½ hours**, plus a short break.
Afterward, we'll take some time to relax, eat, and enjoy each other's company.

***

## 🍁 Fall Weather & Expectations

This is a **moderately challenging hike**, not a casual stroll.
There are hills, uneven sections, and some ups and downs, so good walking or hiking shoes are important.
Please come prepared for typical fall weather and bring enough water for the hike.

If you're comfortable walking for a couple of hours and handling some elevation changes, you'll be fine.
If you're looking for something completely flat and easy, **this probably isn't the walk for you.**

***

## 🚌 Meetup Details

### 🚇 By TTC

📍 **Meetup Location:** Don Mills Station — on the platform for the **85C bus**
🫎 **Look for me in my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time:** **9:45 AM**
🚌 **Bus Leaves:** **10:06 AM sharp**
I'll wait for the bus, but if you miss it, **you won't be able to join the group afterward.**
**Early is on time. On time is late.**

### 🚗 By Car

Parking is **not available at our TTC meeting point.**

If you're driving, please park at the **Toronto Zoo** and walk to the **Park's Welcome Centre (the house)**.
🚗 **Car Meetup Time:** 11:00 AM

We may be a few minutes late arriving, depending on the bus and traffic.

***

## 🧺 The Picnic

After the hike, we'll have a **30–40 minute group picnic** at the end.
Please bring something small to share — nothing too large or heavy. The goal is simply to have something to eat together after the hike.
🥪 Sandwiches
🍎 Fruit
🍪 Snacks
🥤 Drinks
Whatever is easy to carry and share is perfect.

***

## 🧢 Meetup Details at a Glance

🥾 **Hike:** Approximately 2½ hours + short break
🧺 **Picnic:** 30–40 minutes
🏁 **End Point:** Park's Welcome Centre
💲 **Meetup Fee:** $5 cash or e-transfer
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**

***

## 🎒 What to Bring

💧 Water
🥾 Good walking shoes or hiking shoes
🥪 A snack
🧺 Something small to share for the picnic
🧥 A fall jacket or layers

***

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This hike is great for:

* People who enjoy a little challenge
* Anyone who wants to explore Rouge National Urban Park
* People who love fall colours 🍂
* Hikers looking for a social outing
* Anyone comfortable walking hills and uneven terrain
* People who want to meet others while getting outside

This isn't the easiest walk we do.
**But sometimes the harder walks are the ones you remember.**

You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**

Questions? Post on the event wall or email **torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com**

**Come for the hike.**
**Stay for the picnic.**
**Leave with a new connection — and maybe a new friend.** 🍂💛

title: Lost Libraries of the Ancient World (LECTURES - 5TH ANNIVERSARY SPECIAL)
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

**The location of this Lecture might change in the next few months so stay tuned for more information regarding the venue! As of now the location will still be Old City Hall at the northeast corner of Queen Street West and Bay Street until further notice.**

We have an amazing "Lecture on the Go" series for 2026/2027. New topics and fascinating stories abound! Join me, and uncover the world and keep active, warm and cool during the winter and summer months!

I started this walking classroom when we were under that horrible cloud called Covid. This series was popular and helped people get back into society and life. The first Lecture on the Go was **Walking North America** and that was in October of 2021. Hard to believe it's been 5 years of lectures. So I wanted to do something special to celebrate 5 years of exploration.

The "Lecture on the Go" Series is open to members who have purchased the YEARLY MEMBERSHIP PASS, it's free for those members. If you wish to attend a lecture and you are not a yearly pass member then the price **per** lecture is $20.00.

Let's get started.

What if some of humanity's greatest discoveries were made thousands of years ago, and then lost forever?

What if entire histories, scientific breakthroughs, literary masterpieces, and eyewitness accounts of the ancient world once existed, only to disappear into the flames of war, and the collapse of civilizations?

Join me for a fascinating journey into the world's lost libraries, from the legendary Library of Alexandria to the vanished collections of ancient empires whose treasures may be lost forever.

At the heart, stands the Library of Alexandria, the most famous library in history. Founded over two thousand years ago, it sought to gather all the knowledge of the known world. Scholars from across the Mediterranean came to study astronomy, mathematics, geography, medicine, philosophy, and literature. Yet one of history's greatest mysteries remains: what happened to this remarkable institution, and what priceless knowledge disappeared with it?

Was it destroyed in a single catastrophe, or did it slowly fade away over centuries from neglect?

Beyond Alexandria, we will explore a forgotten world of lost libraries and vanished collections stretching from Mesopotamia and ancient Egypt to medieval Europe, Baghdad, and China. Discover the remarkable stories of librarians, scholars, explorers, and rulers who dedicated their lives to preserving knowledge.

We will encounter lost books, missing histories, ancient scientific works, and literary treasures that survive today only as fragments.
This lecture is an exploration of one of history's most compelling questions: What have we forgotten?

And how libraries shaped civilization and why their loss continues to fascinate us centuries later. Whether you are a lover of history, literature, archaeology, or simply enjoy a good mystery, this special Lecture on the Go will leave you wondering. What secrets of the past may still lie hidden, just waiting to be rediscovered? Fascinating indeed!

Upcoming topics in the 2026 series:

\*Philosophy 1: Great Minds of the Western World: Goethe to Kant! - (2027)
\*Philosophy 2: Great Minds of the Eastern
World: Chuang Tzu to Dalai Lama - (2027)
Legacy of Triangle: How a New York Factory Scandal changed North America - (September 2027)

So book your plans now!

This event is for all levels and walkers, there are a few steps here and there to navigate, but mostly on one level. This event in a non-walking event.

The lecture begins on the steps of Old City Hall at the northeast corner of Bay Street and Queen Street West, and
has a ticket price of $20.00 per person, but **free with the yearly membership pass**.

**Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

Everyone who attends will design a piece of clothing, make the pattern, prepare the fabric, cut the pieces, and hand-stitch it together in a 3-hour period. About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature-focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.

A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

Linda is a Toronto-based artist, specializing in watercolour painting techniques. title: The Sultan and the Detective: Sherlock Holmes’ Curious Adventures in the Ottoman Empire
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall, Ground floor
description:
The Friends of the Arthur Conan Doyle Collection: 2026 Cameron Hollyer Memorial Lecture
Historical fact: the last great Ottoman sultan, Abdülhamid II, fell asleep each night to the adventures of Sherlock Holmes, read aloud to him by a palace attendant. This unlikely obsession is the starting point for Andrew Finkel's novel
The Adventure of the Second Wife.
In this talk, Finkel explores how the world of Arthur Conan Doyle intersected with the late Ottoman Empire, and what this reveals about storytelling, translation, and the unexpected ways stories travel across languages, cultures, and empires to take on meanings the author never intended.
Andrew Finkel is a journalist and author who has reported from Turkey for major international outlets including
The Times, The Economist, TIME, CNN,
and
The New York Times
. He co-founded Platform24 (P24), an Istanbul-based NGO that supports independent journalism and freedom of expression, and is the author of
Turkey: What Everyone Needs to Know
.
Admission is Free. All are welcome. Please note, refreshments will be provided at this event.

title: Série Portraits et autoportraits: Quand la représentation sociale cède la place aux sentiments.
description:
Du Néoclassicisme à l’Académisme, de David à Ingres, les commandes de portraits furent souvent le moyen d’affirmer son rang dans la société. Du Romantisme à l’Impressionnisme, une sensibilité nouvelle se fait jour : l’on pose en communion avec la nature et non plus dans la magnificence de sa demeure, les regards traduisent des sentiments (Renoir) et non plus une volonté de puissance, les gestes sont spontanés (Degas, Manet) et non plus codifiés. Quant aux artistes, ils valorisent, dans leurs autoportraits, l’acte créateur, l’inspiration (Girodet, Delacroix), voire les tourments intérieurs (Courbet, Baudelaire).
Cette conférence vous est proposée par Gilles Genty, historien de l’art, en partenariat avec l’
Alliance française de Toronto
.

Le sous-titrage en direct ou automatique, l’interprétation en langue des signes, les services d’intervenant, ou les services d’accompagnement sont disponibles sur demande. Veuillez soumettre votre demande au moins deux semaines à l’avance à : tpl.ca/accessibility-events

title: Water Marbling Bookmarks Workshop
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Immerse yourself in the mesmerizing world of water marbling — an ancient technique of floating pigments on water and transferring them onto paper to create intricate, fluid designs.

Practiced for centuries across the Islamic world, particularly in regions such as Türkiye, Iran, and the Indian subcontinent, water marbling has been used to adorn calligraphy, manuscripts, and decorative papers. In this introductory workshop, you will explore its rich history and cultural significance while mastering traditional tools and methods to produce a variety of classic patterns. Guided step-by-step, you will create between five and eight unique marbled bookmarks to take home — each a one-of-a-kind reflection of colour, movement, and your own creative expression.

description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

Muddy York, Toronto after 1834 was a **not so innocent** little town as one might think.

It had its share of death and destruction. arson, murder, plenty of murder, and ghost sightings after these events. Wild stories to tell children around the camp fire. But these stories are true. Join me on a walk around old Toronto, and prepare for the Halloween season just ahead.

Have you heard about the Mad Dog of Jarvis street? Or what happened in the old York Town Hall on a day when William Lyon was about to pull the curtain down on the Family Compact, you could say it got very sticky, very quickly.

And after this you could say that people were hooked on all the stories. You could also say that people got hung up on William. Ok enough fun talk, let's go exploring. A walking tour into the dark heart and secrets of the Toronto we all love so much.

Stories that will make your Halloween! And chill your blood. Sounds like a plan!

Let's explore stories of Toronto's bloodiest side!

This walking tour is for all levels and walkers. This tour is for children over the age of 12!

The tour begins on the steps of the Yorkville Library on Yorkville Avenue just west of Yonge Street. The tour ends at King Street East, and Church Street.

And just look for me. I'll be there, or at least my spirit will be.......

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: Fall Exhibition Kickoff
description:
Date: Sunday, October 25, 2026
Time: 12:00 pm to 4:00 pm
Location: Bata Shoe Museum
Tickets: Included with General Admission 
Celebrate the opening of our fall exhibition, Brilliant: The Art of Beaded Footwear around the World — an exhibition spanning 400 years of history and five corners of the globe, from Indigenous North America and West Africa to South and Southeast Asia, Europe, and Western fashion. 
Join us for a full afternoon of family-friendly fun, with guided tours through over 85 extraordinary objects, hands-on beading crafts for all ages, and conversations with artists who have dedicated their practice to this meticulous, centuries-old art form. Discover how a single bead — fragile, painstaking, and deeply symbolic — has adorned footwear across cultures, and explore what the future of this remarkable craft might look like. 
A perfect day out for the whole family. Come curious, leave inspired!

title: Paradise Opening Night Reception
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
In the multimedia exhibit, Paradise , which includes sculpture, print, and video, Japanese Canadian artists and childhood friends Emma Nishimura and Mitchell Akiyama grapple with their family histories of internment. They consider how utopian worlds are created through resilience and displacement, while urging us to remember that utopia for some may not be utopia for all. Find out more about the exhibit here . Please join us at our opening reception for a chance to take in this meaningful show and to meet the artists! Light refreshments will be served.

title: Embroidery and Watercolor Workshop
location: Cedarvale Park,443 Arlington Avenue, York, ON M6C 3A2, Canada
description:
A beginner-friendly workshop where you'll learn the basics of embroidery and discover how to incorporate watercolour with embroidery to create charming, fall-inspired designs.

No prior experience required; come as you are, and all materials are provided. By the end of the session, you'll take home a cute, small piece of fabric art that you made yourself!

What you'll learn

  * Embroidery basics: Get familiar with embroidery hoops, needles, threads, and how to prepare your fabric.
  * Two foundational stitches: Learn the back stitch and French knot, and practice using them to create simple motifs.
  * Watercolour on fabric: Learn how to use watercolour to create soft washes and colourful backgrounds on fabric.
  * Combining paint & thread: Explore how watercolour and embroidery can work together, and use your painted fabric as a canvas for your stitches.
  * Create your own fall-inspired piece: Bring everything together to embroider a cute autumn or Halloween-inspired motif — think pumpkins, apples, ghosts, and more!

title: Ghosts of West Toronto - Halloween Event 2026
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

Halloween is the best time to take in the ghosts that haunt our minds and our city. The city is not quite asleep yet and things roam. They cross our paths with the stories we tell. At the core of this tour, two brutal stories that have impacted Toronto, are explored, but have a ghostly following. You could say this tour explores the old stories that stir the blood, even after 150 years.

Toronto is not a squeaky clean polished town, it has plenty to chill the blood. Stories of horror and crime and things that go bump in the night abound.

From the true horror of the Mercer Reformatory to the Central Prison in Liberty Village, and the ghosts of the exhibition grounds, things that should be left alone will be dug up.

Many other unexplained happenings will be talked about, this tour will haunt, or at least you hope so! Well let's get through this one alive.

This walking tour is for all levels and walkers. The tour begins at the TTC Exhibition Streetcar loop at the corner of Dufferin Street, and Springhurst Avenue in Parkdale.

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

Hope to see you there. And at the end of the tour hopefully you are still around. Well maybe.....

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

title: Guilhem Lavaux (University of Waterloo)
location: MP1318A
description:
Title: From Galaxy Catalogs to the Initial Conditions: Building a Digital Twin of the Nearby Universe

Abstract: In our current cosmological paradigm, every observable structure, from the Milky Way to massive galaxy clusters, grew from a specific realization of primordial gravitational-potential fluctuations. Can we infer the realization that gave rise to the galaxies we observe? And can we evolve it forward to obtain a physical "digital twin" of our cosmic neighborhood?

Modern surveys, including Rubin-LSST, Euclid and DESI, are now mapping millions to billions of galaxies. However, cosmological analyses still rely mostly on two-point statistics, discarding much of the small-scale information. Field-level inference, developed over the past fifteen years, follows a different route: it forward-models the full three-dimensional galaxy field and samples the primordial fluctuations directly.

In this talk, I will present the Manticore digital twins, inferred with the BORG (Bayesian Origin Reconstruction from Galaxies) framework. Manticore-Local is built from the 2M++ galaxy compilation. Manticore-Deep adds the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) to reach redshift 0.7 in a 4 Gpc/h box. A Local Group sibling focuses on the Milky Way and M31. I will first explain what goes into these reconstructions and where the models fall short. I will then show how we validate the twins against independent data, such as cluster masses and galaxy distances. Finally, I will discuss the new answers and new problems emerging from them: the impact on local measurements of the Hubble constant, the mass of the Local Group, and new challenges for the subgrid models of hydrodynamical simulations such as the FLAMINGO suite.

title: Author Talk featuring Sally Hayden
location: Ben McNally Books
description:
[at Ben McNally Books]
Join us at Ben McNally Books for a special evening with journalist Sally Hayden, former winner of the Irish Book of the Year (
My Fourth Time, We Drowned
), and author of
This is Also a Love Story: A Reporter's Search for Goodness in a Cruel World
.
Sally with be joined in conversation by journalist Katie Engelhart.
Order a copy of
This is Also a Love Story
here.
About the Book
An acclaimed reporter takes us on an unforgettable journey, capturing the human capacity for love and connection against all odds.
We live in an era defined by crisis—whether it be war and displacement, climate collapse, or growing inequality, and how the powerful profit from violence and exploitation. Celebrated foreign correspondent Sally Hayden has spent her career on the frontlines, uncovering some of the darkest moments of our time. Yet even in the face of unimaginable adversity, she’s witnessed the incredible goodness of regular people.
In
This Is Also a Love Story
, Hayden reexamines catastrophe through the love stories she has come across. She introduces us to a mother in northeast Nigeria who risks everything to save her daughter from forced marriage to Boko Haram militants, and to a group of Syrian women who have tirelessly searched for their missing spouses and children, while launching a call for justice. We meet a couple separated by the Russian invasion of Ukraine and read letters from the bereaved to the dead, still being written over a decade after the tsunami that devastated Japan. Through these stories, which crisscross the globe, from Uganda to Lebanon, Ghana, Rwanda and Iraq, she challenges us to reconsider what it means to be alive on this planet today.
What if news was recounted through the prism of the actions and decisions people take for those they love? Would it become harder to dehumanize those who seem different to us?
This Is Also a Love Story
dares us to recognize how innate generosity and self-sacrifice can be found in even the most difficult of times, and—as a result—to question what might be needed to create a better world.
About the Author
Sally Hayden is an Irish journalist focused on migration, conflict, and humanitarian crises. Sally’s work has been featured by
The New York Times, the Irish Times, The Washington Post, Financial Times, The Guardian, CNN International, Al Jazeera, Time, BBC
, and other outlets across the world. Sally’s first book
My Fourth Time, We Drowned
was the winner of the Orwell Prize and the Irish Book of the Year, and was a finalist for the Baillie Gifford Prize and the New York Public Library’s Helene Bernstein Book Award for excellence in journalism.

title: Festival Select: Mad Love (1935) and Mark of the Vampire (1935)
location: North York Central Library, Room 101
description:
Join the Society and Recreation department of the North York Central Library for monthly screenings of fiction and non-fiction films that push the boundaries of the medium. This month we are showing
Mad Love
